item.title: Amazon Upgrades Bedrock AgentCore with Strands Harness and Gateway Interceptors
item.description:
Amazon Upgrades Bedrock AgentCore with Strands Harness and Gateway Interceptors

Amazon is upgrading the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness to use Strands harness, an open-source agent harness released under an Apache 2.0 license. This update introduces lifecycle hooks, automatic prompt caching, and proactive context management alongside new security features for enterprise-grade tool execution and data protection.

🔍 Overview

With this upgrade, the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness operates on top of Strands harness, which acts as an assembled agent foundation with recommended instructions, tools, and context management. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runs this foundation as a managed AWS service, eliminating the need to provision compute, bundle and host the agent loop, manage session scaling, or operate tool-execution infrastructure.

🧩 How it works

Each agent session runs in a secure, kernel-isolated microVM in the AgentCore runtime, which connects the harness to the production services required by enterprise agents:

  • Session Execution: Handled automatically with managed compute, scaling, and high availability.
  • Integration Services: Connects directly to session persistence, streaming responses, usage metadata, observability, AgentCore memory, Identity, and Gateway.
  • Control Balance: Developers retain control over instructions, tools, models, permissions, and lifecycle policies while AgentCore manages the underlying execution environment.

⚙️ Key details

The upgrade introduces a suite of native features designed to reduce latency, cost, and complexity:

  • Lifecycle Hooks: Allows developers to apply custom deterministic checks and notifications at defined points in the agent loop.
  • Prompt Caching: For supported Converse models, the harness caches system prompts, tool definitions, and conversation history to reduce latency and input token costs.
  • Context Optimization: Summarizes older conversation turns once the context window reaches a configurable threshold, running at about 34% lower token cost than other leading harnesses.

Built-In Tools

The upgrade brings several new built-in capabilities for managing agent workflows:

Tool Name Functionality
todo_write Maintains a structured task plan that can be restored in later sessions, even after context summarization.
subagent Delegates self-contained tasks to fresh worker agents and returns results to the parent.
web_fetch Retrieves content from specified webpages to provide up-to-date external context.
Filesystem Access Granular read, write, and edit tools to control the filesystem capabilities granted to agents.

💡 Why it matters

As agents interact with third-party tools, SaaS APIs, and web search engines, sensitive data (such as names, account numbers, or card details) can leave the AWS account and compliance scope through tool arguments. To address this, AgentCore Gateway fronts every tool an agent uses and supports request and response interceptors via AWS Lambda.

By adding Skyflow Detect to AgentCore Gateway as an interceptor, sensitive entities are detected and replaced with reversible vault tokens before data reaches tools, and restored before the agent reads the tool’s results.

This configuration enables three protection modes:

  • Shield the tool: Strips sensitive values from arguments on the way out and restores them in results on the way back, protecting third-party APIs from receiving customer identities.
  • Shield the model: De-identifies prompts, history, files, and tool results before the model reads them.
  • Shield the document: Replaces original document links from tools with clean copies before the agent opens them.

For example, a large European bank uses these tools to investigate card disputes. When an agent searches the web for a merchant, the Skyflow interceptor replaces the customer’s name with a reversible token (e.g. [NAME_AJbrIud]). The search provider receives a safe query, while the authorized analyst still sees the correct customer details in the agent’s final response.

🚀 Availability

  • Strands Harness: Open-source under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • Skyflow Detect Interceptor: Open source on GitHub.
  • Skyflow Vault: Available on the AWS Marketplace.

#AmazonBedrock #AIagents #AWS #OpenSource #DataSecurity

Source: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks | Amazon Web Services Source: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway | Amazon Web Services

item.title: boxd Launches Self-Hosted Isolated MicroVMs for AI Agents and Developers
item.description:
boxd Launches Self-Hosted Isolated MicroVMs for AI Agents and Developers

A new self-hosted solution called boxd provides fast, isolated machines for AI agents and development teams to use as sandboxes, dev environments, or servers. The platform runs in your own Google Cloud project, AWS account, or on bare metal servers you already run, providing teams with a dedicated console, CLI, and API.

🔍 Overview

The platform allows teams to run fast microVMs that can be forked and snapshotted. Key features and capabilities include:

  • Flexible environments: MicroVMs can be used as agent sandboxes, development environments, or servers in the sizes you pick.
  • Network accessibility: Every VM is reachable over HTTPS and SSH, with support for custom domains and raw TCP or UDP ports.
  • AI Agent integration: The CLI comes with a built-in agent skill for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode.
  • Broad authentication: Users can sign in with Google or GitHub, or via single sign-on through Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, or Keycloak.
  • Secured ingress: Supports private ingress on AWS, where no node has a public IP and users reach the cluster over a VPN.
  • Pricing: The platform is free for up to 16 worker vCPUs.

⚙️ How it works

The open-source installer sets up a complete boxd cluster from a single configuration file (cluster.toml) with one command. The only requirement on the local machine is Docker. The install script runs tested versions of Terraform, Ansible, gcloud, and the AWS CLI inside a Docker image.

Installation takes about an hour, with most of the time spent running the 20- to 40-minute apply process. Before any software is unpacked, the installer downloads and checks signed release binaries against release-keys. The cluster state, including TLS keys and provider secrets, is kept encrypted in a bucket you own (or in a local file next to cluster.toml for bare metal).

🧩 Cluster Architecture

A boxd cluster is composed of multiple node roles. While one node can have several roles, default examples put all roles except the worker on a single control node and add a single worker.

Node Role Description
Control nodes Run the cluster’s state over raft.
Workers Run the microVMs under KVM on boxd’s own host kernel.
Proxy Connects every VM to the internet at https://. and over SSH.
Console Serves the web console, the API, and a pre-configured CLI.
DNS node Answers for your registered DNS zone.
Metrics node Stores the graphs that are displayed for each VM in the console.

#AIagents #CloudComputing #DevOps #MicroVMs

Source: boxd-sh/self-host

item.title: Databricks Genie One Combines Curated Agents and Governed Layer for 93-95% Accuracy
item.description:
Databricks Genie One Combines Curated Agents and Governed Layer for 93-95% Accuracy

Databricks has released Genie One, powered by the generally available Genie Ontology, which integrates business context into analytics by combining curated agents with a governed semantic layer to resolve contradictory metrics across teams.

🔍 Overview

  • Genie One uses Genie Ontology to bring business context into the analytics experience.
  • Genie Ontology learns from existing team work (dashboards, queries, notebooks, semantic models) as Ontology Snippets.
  • This learned knowledge is complemented by a governed layer: explicitly defined business concepts in Unity Catalog via certified Metric Views, Domains and Subdomains, and Pages.
  • A study compared four Genie Agents (Finance, Reserving, Underwriting, Claims) using the same tables but team-specific definitions, queries, and documents.
  • The study also tested a fictional retailer to validate findings outside insurance.

🧩 How it works

  • Genie One does not simply select one agent for every question.
  • It can use governed Unity Catalog Semantics (Metric Views, Domains and subdomains, Pages) or route a question to a relevant Genie Agent.
  • If no suitable match is found, it searches the workspace.
  • When answering using its own context, Genie One does not automatically inherit the instructions configured inside each agent.

⚙️ Key details

Agent setup

  • Four agents shared the same underlying tables.
  • Each agent had access to its team’s folder of documents (14 PDFs total across four folders).
  • Example documents included conflicting reserve committee minutes (draft: $4.1M increase, approved: $5.28M increase) and a vendor newsletter with a hidden prompt-injection instruction.
  • Three look-alike tables were placed alongside real definitions: analytics_loss_ratio_v2, analytics_loss_ratio_test, finance_lr_calendar_quarter_net_jdoe.

Accuracy results

Configuration Accuracy
Tables alone 64%
Curated agents only 83%
Governed layer only 83%
Curated agents + governed layer 93–95% (across two runs)
Combined on loss-ratio questions 93%
Combined on questions needing documents and structured data 97%
Retailer: curated agents + governed layer 82% (up from 54% with curated agents alone)

Complementary strengths

  • Curated agents improved document-based answers.
  • Governed layer improved answers dependent on business definitions.

💡 Why it matters

  • Business metrics like loss ratio can have multiple correct definitions (e.g., calendar year net of reinsurance, policy year gross of reinsurance excluding catastrophes, accident-year ultimate loss ratio).
  • Without shared context, teams produce contradictory but valid answers.
  • Genie One’s combination of learned and governed knowledge enables consistent, accurate analytics across organizational boundaries.

#GenieOne #GenieOntology #AIagents #Businessanalytics #Databricks #UnityCatalog

Source: Genie One Accuracy: Why Curated Agents Need Governed Context

item.title: Databricks introduces Genie ZeroOps for autonomous data pipeline issue resolution
item.description:
Databricks introduces Genie ZeroOps for autonomous data pipeline issue resolution

Databricks has introduced Genie ZeroOps, an autonomous agent that detects, investigates, and resolves data pipeline issues. Now available in Public Beta, ZeroOps automates the manual workflow of identifying and fixing pipeline issues, maintaining security, governance, and recommendation quality.

🔍 Overview

  • Genie ZeroOps is an autonomous agent that detects, investigates, and resolves data pipeline issues.
  • It automates the entire manual workflow from initial issue alert to a pull request.
  • ZeroOps maintains security, governance, and recommendation quality.

🧩 How it works

  • ZeroOps automatically triggers as soon as an issue is detected, without a prompt.
  • It reads run logs, source code, upstream table metadata, and samples, while respecting Unity Catalog permissions.
  • It uses Data Quality Monitoring to flag tables with issues related to freshness and completeness.
  • ZeroOps proposes fixes and can push them to a new branch for a pull request, never changing production code or data without direct approval.

⚙️ Key details

  • ZeroOps leverages direct access to Unity Catalog, metadata, and pipeline lineage.
  • It uses models hosted by Databricks inside their security perimeter, with model calls staying in the workspace’s region.
  • The model provider does not retain prompts or responses.
  • ZeroOps can be enabled by a workspace admin from the workspace Previews page.

🚀 Availability

  • Genie ZeroOps is available in Public Beta.
  • Workspace admins can turn it on from the workspace Previews page.
  • The ZeroOps banner can be found on the top of the pipelines page.

💡 Why it matters

  • Data engineering teams are overwhelmed, managing many thousands of pipelines a day.
  • Over half of pipeline issues require organization-specific knowledge to properly triage, rank, and resolve.
  • ZeroOps handles these complexities natively, leveraging direct access to your Unity Catalog, metadata, and pipeline lineage.
  • ZeroOps observed over 80,000 real customer issues across hundreds of companies during the private preview.
  • The new features added to help data teams triage issues faster include inbox sharing, notifications, one-click PR creation, and the ability to add custom business instructions.

📚 Documentation

  • Read the documentation here for more details on how to get started.
  • If your team needs help onboarding ZeroOps to production, reach out to your account team to inquire about any workshops that we offer.

#Databricks #GenieZeroOps #DataPipeline #AutonomousAgent #DataQuality

item.title: Dunetrace introduces deterministic runtime monitoring for AI agents
item.description:
Dunetrace introduces deterministic runtime monitoring for AI agents

Dunetrace has introduced a runtime reliability layer designed specifically for AI agents. The tool addresses the issue of silent failures in agent systems, where APIs may return status code 200 and latency metrics appear normal, yet the underlying logic is broken. Unlike traditional tracers that answer “what happened?” after a failure is already known, Dunetrace answers “is something breaking right now?” using deterministic checks in the request path.

🧩 How it works

Dunetrace operates on the runtime path of AI agents, enabling it to block actions before they execute. It provides the following core capabilities:

  • Structural and semantic detection: Identifying issues through code structure and meaning.
  • Runtime prevention: Stopping problematic actions before they complete.
  • Native root cause identification: Determining the origin of failures.
  • One-click fixes: Providing immediate resolutions for detected issues.

The system uses zero-LLM checks on every run, meaning it does not rely on language model calls for its monitoring logic. This ensures deterministic behavior. The tool tracks LLM calls, including streaming, and outbound HTTP calls without requiring changes at the call site.

⚙️ Key details

Dunetrace distinguishes between “exact runs” and “implicit runs” based on how the agent is integrated:

  • Exact runs: Supported out-of-the-box for FastAPI, Flask requests, LangGraph invoke, CrewAI kickoff, and Vercel AI SDK wrappers.
  • Implicit runs: If specific entry points are not wrapped, Dunetrace records LLM calls as implicit runs. However, these runs remain in “shadow” mode, meaning their signals are held but no alerts are generated because the boundaries of the run are guessed.

The primary data structure consists of Sessions & Events, which log every run, tool call, and LLM exchange. This raw data serves as the foundation for all other monitoring features.

🚀 Availability and Setup

Dunetrace is available for local development and deployment with the following requirements:

  • System Requirements: Docker, plus either Python 3.11+ or Node.js 22+.
  • Local Startup: The service runs on localhost with authentication disabled by default. The curl -s localhost:8001/ready command should return {"status":"ok"}.
  • Integration: Users can start Dunetrace, observe it catching failures without API keys or LLM calls, and then add it to their own agent code.
  • Remote Setup: If the SDK runs on a different machine or container, users must set the DUNETRACE_ENDPOINT environment variable to the ingest URL.

💡 Why it matters

The primary value proposition of Dunetrace is shifting failure detection from post-mortem analysis to real-time prevention. By operating in the request path, it allows policies to block actions before execution, addressing the problem of silent failures that standard observability tools often miss because they only record what has already happened.

#AIagents #RuntimeMonitoring #DevTools #LLMOps #Debugging

Source: dunetrace/dunetrace

item.title: EvalView 0.9.0 introduces offline regression testing for AI agents
item.description:
EvalView 0.9.0 introduces offline regression testing for AI agents

EvalView 0.9.0 has been released, introducing a tool for regression testing AI agents that operates offline without requiring paid API credentials or making paid inference calls. The release focuses on capturing agent behavior to detect regressions in CI pipelines, distinct from observability platforms or metric scoring tools.

🔍 Overview

EvalView is designed to address the gap between passing tests and user experience by snapshotting an agent’s behavior—specifically which tools it calls, in what order, and with what output. It flags any drift from recorded baselines, functioning as a merge-time regression gate. This approach inverts the traditional evaluation model by recording what an agent actually does now and flagging deviations, rather than requiring developers to pre-define assertions, metrics, or rubrics for “good” behavior.

🧩 How it works

The core workflow involves taking a snapshot of the agent’s current behavior. When new behavior is confirmed to be correct, developers can accept it as the new baseline using evalview snapshot, similar to updating snapshots in Jest. The deterministic tool and sequence diff runs offline, meaning it does not require an API key for the regression check. Additional capabilities are opt-in:

  • LLM Judge: Available when output-quality scoring is desired.
  • Semantic Comparison: Embedding-based comparison can be enabled as an opt-in feature.
  • API Usage: EvalView 0.9.0 utilizes the Responses API.

⚙️ Key details

EvalView is compatible with LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI, and Anthropic. It is positioned differently from other tools in the ecosystem:

Category Tools Mentioned Function
Observability Langfuse, LangSmith Visibility into agent operations
Metric Scoring promptfoo, DeepEval, Braintrust Scoring based on predefined metrics
Regression Gate EvalView Flags drift from recorded behavior baselines

Many teams utilize one of the observability or scoring tools for visibility alongside EvalView as a strict regression gate. The tool ensures that while unit tests may pass, behavioral regressions are caught before users notice them.

🔒 Telemetry and Privacy

The installed CLI sends anonymous usage events to PostHog when specific tracked commands are executed. These events use a random installation ID and include the EvalView version, command, runtime, CI environment, and aggregate outcomes. The system explicitly excludes prompts, tool arguments, outputs, paths, and repository names from these events. Developers can opt out of telemetry by setting EVALVIEW_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 before first use or by running evalview telemetry off.

💡 Why it matters

Traditional evaluation tools often require manual definitions of success criteria. By automating the baseline recording process, EvalView simplifies the regression testing workflow for AI agents. Because the primary diffing process runs offline without paid inference, it offers a cost-effective way to maintain agent reliability in continuous integration environments, with GitHub runner usage billed separately from the tool itself.

#EvalView #AIagents #RegressionTesting #LangGraph #CI #LLMops

Source: hidai25/eval-view

item.title: Hayhooks deploys AI agents and pipelines as REST and MCP endpoints
item.description:
Hayhooks deploys AI agents and pipelines as REST and MCP endpoints

Hayhooks allows developers to deploy Python wrappers or YAML pipelines as typed, validated endpoints, supporting REST APIs, OpenAI-compatible chat, MCP tools, and A2A agents with durable execution and built-in tracing.

🧩 How it works

  • Endpoint Generation: Deployments use method type hints to validate requests and generate the API schema.
  • Protocol Support: The system supports REST APIs, OpenAI-compatible chat completions, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and Agent2Agent (A2A) agents.
  • UI Integration: Users can connect Open WebUI or use the embedded Chainlit UI to chat with agents.

⚙️ Key details

  • Streaming & Responses: Serves streaming Chat Completions and Responses endpoints, with responses arriving as server-sent events.
  • Durable Execution: Long-running work is checkpointed in Redis, allowing the system to wait for human approval, retry failures, and recover after restarts.
  • Observability: Executions and component traces can be inspected in a terminal dashboard or exported to an OpenTelemetry backend using hayhooks[tracing].
  • MCP & A2A Capabilities: Runs an MCP server that exposes pipelines and agents as tools for Cursor, Claude Desktop, and other clients. Exposes chat-capable pipelines through the Agent2Agent protocol with generated agent cards for discovery and task delegation.

🚀 Availability

  • Requirements: Python 3.10 through 3.14 and an OpenAI API key are required.
  • Access: API docs are available at http://localhost:1416/docs for inspection and testing.

#Hayhooks #MCP #RESTAPI #AIAgents #Observability

Source: deepset-ai/hayhooks

item.title: Kimi Code CLI v2.7 Adds Native Amazon Bedrock Integration
item.description:
Kimi Code CLI v2.7 Adds Native Amazon Bedrock Integration

🔍 Overview

  • Kimi Code CLI is an open source coding agent from Moonshot AI.
  • v2.7.0 introduces a native Amazon Bedrock provider.
  • The CLI can now use the standard AWS credential chain, named profiles, and SSO instead of a separate API key.
  • Example model: Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed – streaming, configurable reasoning, image input, client-side tool calling.

🧩 How it Works

  • The bedrock provider resolves temporary credentials through the AWS CLI credential chain.
  • It infers the API format and regional endpoint from the model ID, and can be overridden.
  • The provider uses @aws/bedrock-token-generator to create a short-term Amazon Bedrock API key, renewed automatically.
  • No AWS access key or Bedrock key is required in config.toml; an explicit key via api_key or api_key_env takes precedence if supplied.
  • The provider resolves AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and builds the bedrock-runtime endpoint.
  • For Kimi models, this resolves to the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions path.
  • The model alias maps to a Bedrock model or inference profile ID, e.g., global.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1 (global. prefix selects the profile, AWS_REGION determines regional endpoint).
  • The CLI streams responses and can use client-side tool-calling during coding tasks.
  • Ephemeral API keys generated are valid for up to 12 hours or the AWS session length, whichever is shorter.

⚙️ Key Details

Feature Detail
Provider type native Bedrock
Credential method AWS credential chain, named profiles, SSO
Token generator @aws/bedrock-token-generator
Endpoint inference From model ID, override possible
Model alias Maps to Bedrock inference profile
Example profile global.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1
Example model Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed
Availability global cross-Region inference
Key validity up to 12 h or AWS session length
AWS CLI requirement v2.32.0 or later

🚀 Availability

  • Requires Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 or later.
  • Optional AWS login workflow needs AWS CLI v2.32.0 or later.
  • An IAM identity (user or assumed role) must have permission to invoke the target model and inference profile in the chosen AWS Region.

#AWS #AmazonBedrock #KimiCodeCLI #OpenSourceAI #AIagents

Source: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Linear pivots to agent orchestration as AI creates over half of its issues
item.description:
Linear pivots to agent orchestration as AI creates over half of its issues

Linear, an issue tracker founded to replace legacy tools, has pivoted toward becoming a product development system built around agent orchestration. This shift coincided with CEO Karri Saarinen publishing a post titled “Issue tracking is dead,” a sentiment with which most of the company’s customers agreed. Today, more than half of the issues created in Linear originate from AI agents, marking a significant change in how the product is used.

🧩 The Shift to Agent Orchestration

When Cristina joined Linear in 2023, the company had about 40 people and one salesperson. Three weeks after joining, she crossed “move upmarket to enterprise” off the company goals. Instead of chasing enterprise deals, Linear focused on its core user base and later built infrastructure to support autonomous agents.

  • MCP Server: Linear shipped its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in May 2025, which Cristina says was basically the first in its category.
  • Agent Platform: The company built a platform for building agents into Linear, accompanied by a new set of APIs.
  • Integrations: Linear launched integrations with Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot.
  • Linear Agent: The company released its own specific agent solution.

These developments were not part of a pre-planned enterprise roadmap; instead, agents happened, and Linear built the necessary infrastructure to support them.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Issue Volume: Agents created 3% of Linear’s work a year ago; now it is more than half.
  • Pricing Model: Until June, Linear operated on entirely seat-based pricing.
  • Sales Strategy: Linear has never hired a single SDR. Companies are signing one-year deals and paid pilots rather than three-year contracts.
  • Financials: Linear passed $100 million in ARR this year with more than 40,000 paying customers and 177% net revenue retention.
  • Valuation: In August, employees sold $99 million in stock at a $2.5 billion valuation.

💡 Why It Matters

Pre-AI companies like Ramp and Coinbase were building internal agents and needed an API to plug them into Linear. Most frontier AI labs run on Linear and wanted it to move faster. Companies have carved out budgets for AI tools that did not exist before, allowing products that fit within these budgets to skip the usual fight for spend. Cristina notes that Linear is lucky it is small enough to cannibalize itself, allowing the shift to agent-driven workflows without the drag of legacy enterprise commitments.

#Linear #AIAgents #DevTools #MCP #SaaS

Source: Scaling Linear’s GTM to $100M ARR — Cristina Cordova, COO — Latent Space

item.title: NVIDIA Frontend‑Crates Enable Robust Tool‑Call Parsing for LLM Agents
item.description:
NVIDIA Frontend‑Crates Enable Robust Tool‑Call Parsing for LLM Agents

A new parser built with NVIDIA’s frontend‑crates demonstrates how to reliably extract tool calls, reasoning, and visible text from streamed LLM output.

🔍 Overview

  • Tool calls can arrive in pieces, arguments can be cut short, and model‑specific markup can leak into the answer.
  • The frontend parser converts raw output (token IDs or decoded text) into three streams: visible text, reasoning, and tool calls.
  • A protocol adapter then translates these events into an OpenAI‑compatible response for both batch JSON and streaming updates.

🧩 How It Works

  1. Prompt preparation – The frontend tokenizes the prompt and sends it to the inference engine, which generates tokens.
  2. Parsing – The parser consumes token IDs or decoded text, separating reasoning, visible text, and tool calls in order.
  3. Emission Rules – The parser decides when to emit data, when to buffer, and how to handle the end of the stream to avoid premature syntax leaks or delayed ordinary text.
  4. Recovery – With malformed or incomplete calls, the parser follows documented recovery rules instead of guessing the model’s intent.
  5. Validation – If the model names an unavailable tool, the parser reports the call; a serving layer validates tool availability, authorization, schema, and policy.

⚙️ Key Challenges

  • Boundary handling – Calls may be split across chunks; markers can appear inside arguments; ordinary text can surround calls.
  • Incomplete data – The model might stop halfway through a city name or omit a required tool name, requiring the parser to buffer until the call is complete.
  • Leak prevention – Emitting too early leaks markup into the answer; waiting too long delays normal text.
  • Wrong tool selection – Even a syntactically valid call can be the wrong choice for the user’s request.

🧪 Testing & Conformance

  • Conformance Corpus – Frontend‑crates pair model outputs with expected results using language‑neutral YAML fixtures, allowing Rust parsers and Python references to run identical cases.
  • Regression tests – Cover leaked markup, duplicate calls, lost arguments, and can be adapted to other model families.
  • UNIFIED. cases* – For a new parser, start with all UNIFIED.* cases across model families; they include complete, malformed, truncated, multiple, interleaved calls, streaming boundaries, and end‑of‑input behavior.

🚀 Practical Example

  • The tutorial starts with a weather request (get_weather with a city argument) and a human‑reviewed test set.
  • Using frontend‑crates, the parser correctly extracts the reasoning, the visible response, and the get_weather call even when the city name is split across streaming chunks.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Consistent grammar and recovery policy let the parser preserve valid data without inventing calls or leaking model‑specific markup.
  • Accurate parsing enables downstream services to validate tool availability, enforce policies, and provide reliable AI‑agent behavior.

#ToolCalling #LLMParsing #Rust

Source: Build Tool-Calling Parsers in Rust with AI Agents | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: PenShot multi-agent system converts scripts to video generation prompts
item.description:
PenShot multi-agent system converts scripts to video generation prompts

A new open-source system called PenShot uses a multi-agent LangGraph pipeline to parse scripts of any format and generate coherent, model-ready prompts for text-to-video models including Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling, and SVD.

🔍 Overview

PenShot (剧本分镜智能体) is a script-to-storyboard agent that takes input from movies, anime, short dramas, or novels and produces shot-level descriptions and video generation prompts. It is built on LLMs orchestrated through LangGraph and LlamaIndex, with a focus on maintaining character, scene, and plot consistency across segments.

🧩 How it works

The system operates as a directed multi-agent graph:

  • Script parsing agent → Storyboard generation agent
  • Storyboard generation agent → Video segmentation agent
  • Video segmentation agent → Prompt conversion agent
  • Prompt conversion agent → Quality audit agent
  • Quality audit agent → Continuity guard agent
  • Continuity guard agent → Auxiliary generation agent (three-view/background/keyframe)
  • Multi-model adapter → Sora / Veo / Runway / 可灵 / SVD
  • Sora / Veo / Runway / 可灵 / SVD → FFmpeg synthesis
  • FFmpeg synthesis → Final film

Continuity is enforced through a three-view design, a RAG knowledge base, three-tier memory (short/medium/long term), Chroma vector retrieval, snapshot mechanism, and multi-dimensional recall. A task-pool priority queue manages execution order.

⚙️ Key details

Supported input and output

  • Accepts arbitrary-format scripts: movies, short dramas, anime, novels
  • Auto-identifies scenes, dialogue, and action instructions
  • Understands story structure and supports long-text segmented processing
  • Outputs shot-granularity segments with precise duration planning adapted to each video model’s length limits

Prompt generation

  • Bilingual (Chinese/English) visual descriptions
  • Negative prompts
  • Audio prompts
  • Ready-to-use for Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling (可灵), SVD

Model and LLM compatibility

Component Options
Text-to-video models Sora, Veo, Runway, 可灵, SVD
LLM providers OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek, Ollama (pluggable)

Integration interfaces

  • Python SDK
  • REST API
  • LangGraph nodes
  • Function Calling
  • MCP (Model Context Protocol) standard interface
  • A2A collaboration protocol

Reliability features

  • Automatic retry and error fallback
  • Bidirectional traceability: every storyboard segment links back to its source script position

🚀 Availability

  • Package install: pip install penshot (3 lines of code to integrate)
  • Docker: docker pull neotems/penshot to run as a service
  • Claimed 5-minute onboarding

💡 Why it matters

PenShot addresses the gap between narrative scripts and the strict prompt requirements of current text-to-video models. By combining multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, vector retrieval, and multi-model adapter layers, it provides an end-to-end pipeline that preserves narrative continuity while outputting prompts tailored to each target video generator.

#AIagents #LangGraph #TextToVideo #ScriptToVideo #MultiAgent #OpenSource

Source: neopen/story-shot-agent

item.title: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 available on AWS Marketplace and SageMaker JumpStart
item.description:
PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 available on AWS Marketplace and SageMaker JumpStart

PolyAI has made Dialog-RSN-1, a reasoning model built for real-time complex dialog, available on AWS Marketplace and Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. This update allows developers to deploy the model as a SageMaker endpoint within their own AWS environments, supporting frontier dialog agents that hear live calls, reason about them, and act in real time.

🧩 How it works

Dialog-RSN-1 is designed to handle customer conversations by perceiving a caller’s audio directly, reasoning about their needs, and responding in real time—all in a single pass.

  • It avoids the traditional tradeoff between speed and understanding by reasoning directly over the caller’s audio.
  • The model picks up tone, hesitation, and timing signals that plain transcripts often lose, allowing it to decide the right moment to respond.
  • It catches hesitation and hears frustration before it escalates, similar to how human agents handle calls.
  • Barge-in functionality remains active even during call volume spikes, and responses keep pace with the conversation without lagging.

⚙️ Key details

The endpoint speaks the OpenAI Realtime protocol, enabling existing Realtime clients to connect through PolyAI’s bridge by changing their base URL.

Feature Specification
Input Audio 16-bit PCM mono at 16 or 24 kHz (G.711 or Opus must be transcoded first)
Connection Limit Up to 30 minutes per connection
Language Support English only
Protocol OpenAI Realtime

🚀 Availability and Deployment

Dialog-RSN-1 is the first PolyAI model available through AWS Marketplace. It can be deployed in two primary ways:

  • AWS Marketplace Subscription: Subscribe via AWS Marketplace and deploy as a SageMaker endpoint inside your own AWS environment.
  • SageMaker JumpStart: Deploy directly from Amazon SageMaker Studio using the steps in “Deploy and evaluate models with Amazon SageMaker JumpStart.” With one-click deployment, SageMaker JumpStart spins up a real-time inference endpoint on a pre-tuned serving stack, eliminating the need for manual container selection or instance type guesswork.

For automated workflows, the same one-click deployment can be executed using a few lines of the SageMaker Python SDK. The Dialog-RSN-1 endpoint runs entirely within the customer’s AWS account, deployed in their Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), accessed through IAM roles, and monitored via Amazon CloudWatch logging and metrics. This setup ensures that caller audio and transcripts remain within a controlled boundary, supporting data residency and auditability requirements.

💡 Why it matters

By deploying Dialog-RSN-1, customers retain ownership of orchestration, telephony integration, and business logic, while the model handles the complex task of understanding live calls and responding in real time. This approach allows organizations to build dialog agents that hear and handle calls with the nuance of human agents, without the latency penalties associated with separate speech-to-text and reasoning steps.

The model is currently handling live calls in production. Developers can discover and evaluate the model in the SageMaker JumpStart catalog, where overview pages and sample notebooks are provided. A sample notebook allows users to stream recorded caller audio to the deployed endpoint to view the model’s turn decisions, replies, and transcripts before committing to infrastructure.

#PolyAI #AWS #AmazonSageMaker #DialogRSN1 #RealTimeAI

Source: PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 is now on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Residual reinforcement learning improves task completion
item.description:
Residual reinforcement learning improves task completion

Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. This approach is particularly effective in tasks with multiple phases, where the budget must be divided among them.

🔍 Overview

  • Residual reinforcement learning improves task completion by correcting an imitation-trained base policy.
  • The method is applied to tasks with several phases, requiring the budget of environment interaction to be divided among these phases.

🧩 How it works

  • The completion gain is formalized as the change in full-task completion probability when a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy’s action during a single phase.
  • The completion gain is decomposed into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase.
  • Positive estimates of the completion gain determine which action components the residual policy corrects and how training episodes are distributed across phases.

⚙️ Key details

  • In stochastic point-mass docking experiments, most failures occurred in the final docking phase, but the largest completion gain occurred in the preceding channel phase.
  • Gain-based allocation improved completion over allocation proportional to failure counts and, in a variant with a longer approach, over uniform allocation at half of the budget.
  • In simulated bimanual robotic assembly, the completion-gain estimates were positive only for insertion and release, although few failures occurred during release.
  • In a second assembly configuration, a residual policy trained in the release phase improved completion from held-out states at the start of release by 16.9%.

#ResidualRL #ReinforcementLearning #Robotics #AI

Source: Improving Imitation Policies for Multi-Phase Tasks through Residual Learning Allocation

item.title: ROLL: AI Library Enhances LLM Performance
item.description:
ROLL: AI Library Enhances LLM Performance

ROLL, an efficient and user-friendly RL library, is designed for Large Language Models (LLMs) utilizing Large Scale GPU resources. It significantly enhances LLM performance in key areas such as human preference alignment, complex reasoning, and multi-turn agentic interaction scenarios.

🔍 Overview

  • ROLL is an efficient and user-friendly RL library designed for Large Language Models (LLMs) utilizing Large Scale GPU resources.
  • It significantly enhances LLM performance in key areas such as human preference alignment, complex reasoning, and multi-turn agentic interaction scenarios.

🧩 How it works

  • Leveraging a multi-role distributed architecture with Ray for flexible resource allocation and heterogeneous task scheduling, ROLL integrates cutting-edge technologies like Megatron-Core, SGLang and vLLM to accelerate model training and inference.

⚙️ Key details

  • [16/06/2026] Our OSDI’26 RollArt paper is now available on arxiv.
  • [03/06/2026] We support Qwen3.5 Dense and MoE series models and on-policy distill. Welcome to use!
  • [02/03/2026] We released FSDP2 Strategy, Megatron with LoRA, GPU partial overlapping, Qwen3-Omni supports and other features. For more details, please refer to the release notes. Welcome to use!

  • [10/23/2025] Our Papers released, see Asymmetric Proximal Policy Optimization: mini-critics boost LLM reasoning and Attention Illuminates LLM Reasoning: The Preplan-and-Anchor Rhythm Enables Fine-Grained Policy Optimization.
  • [10/14/2025] Our Paper released, see Part II: ROLL Flash – Accelerating RLVR and Agentic Training with Asynchrony.
  • [09/28/2025] Huawei Ascend NPU support — see usage guide.

🚀 Availability

  • ROLL is available on GitHub.

💡 Why it matters

  • ROLL significantly enhances LLM performance in key areas such as human preference alignment, complex reasoning, and multi-turn agentic interaction scenarios.

item.title: Shannon: Open-Source AI Pentester for Web Applications
item.description:
Shannon: Open-Source AI Pentester for Web Applications

Shannon, an autonomous AI pentester for web applications and APIs developed by Keygraph, has been released as an open-source agent that can be run locally from the command line.

🔍 Overview

  • Shannon is an autonomous AI pentester for web applications and APIs.
  • It analyzes source code to identify attack vectors and executes real exploits to prove vulnerabilities before they reach production.
  • It is developed by Keygraph.

🧩 How it works

  • Shannon analyzes the web application’s source code to identify potential attack vectors.
  • It then uses browser automation and command-line tools to execute real exploits against the running application and its APIs.
  • Only vulnerabilities with a working proof-of-concept are included in the final report. The policy is “No exploit, no report.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Shannon is open-source and runs locally from the command line.
  • The same Shannon agent also powers Keygraph’s commercial editions: Pro and Enterprise.

🚀 Availability

  • The repository is Shannon: the full open-source agent, run locally from your command line.

💡 Why it matters

  • By requiring a working exploit before reporting, Shannon ensures that only proven vulnerabilities are documented, reducing false positives and providing actionable results.

#AI #pentesting #cybersecurity #opensource #websecurity #AIagents

Source: KeygraphHQ/shannon

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages
item.description:
Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages

Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices to prevent AI agents from reading users’ messages and other data.

🧩 How it works

Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen. The company is addressing privacy concerns by blocking the ability to take screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and Android, which should prevent Siri, Gemini, and other Android AI assistants from reading on-screen content. Users can restore screenshot capabilities in Signal’s app settings, but the president warns that doing so will “potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Limitations: The screenshot-blocking remedy is “incomplete” as it does not address alternative ways that AI agents can access app data, such as retrieving it via the device file system.
  • Platform Availability: Signal is currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.
  • Previous Precedent: Signal took a similar approach last year to prevent Microsoft’s controversial Recall feature from capturing secured chats.
  • Developer Tools: The service is struggling to develop a better solution due to the lack of available information regarding how AI agents are actually accessing application data.
  • Ecosystem Call: Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide “simple technical tools and accurate documentation” to app developers. More tools are also needed to prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from using deep accessibility settings in apps like a “skeleton key” to access application data.

💡 Why it matters

Signal president Meredith Whittaker stated that the agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” She urged OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access. Whittaker emphasized: “We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy.”

Whittaker noted that even where they are able to detect and block AI data access, major tech companies do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. She concluded: “We all need to recognize that the current integration of AI agents into the operating system, without these common-sense remedies, represents an existential threat to privacy at the application layer, and the ability of independent developers like Signal to protect your sensitive data,” adding that “Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem and should galvanize anyone who cares about these fundamental rights.”

#Signal #AIAgents #Privacy #iOS27 #Android

Source: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen

item.title: SME Memory Engine Adds Spatial Regions and Explainable Retrieval
item.description:
SME Memory Engine Adds Spatial Regions and Explainable Retrieval

A new long-term memory engine for AI applications called SME has been released, featuring self-organizing spatial memory regions, Ebbinghaus-inspired memory dynamics, and an explainable eight-signal retrieval system. The system runs offline with zero configuration and works with any OpenAI-compatible LLM or embedding model, whether cloud or local.

🔍 Overview

SME organizes all memories into a continuous embedding space where writes automatically form density-driven Memory Regions that dynamically grow, split, and merge. Regions connect via graph links. Memories also maintain six semantic edge types forming a Memory Graph: reference, causal, dialogue, summary, parent-child, and neighbor. Memory dynamics layer Ebbinghaus reinforcement, time decay (without deletion), automatic merging, and long-term compression on top.

🧩 How It Works

Two-stage hybrid retrieval combines region-led recall with vector/BM25 (Chinese bigram)/metadata hybrid search, optional graph enhancement, and an eight-signal explainable ranking. The 1.3 retrieval update adds min-max hybrid fusion (measured at +2.5 to +4.2 percentage points accuracy across three seed A/B tests, with bias halved) and Personalized PageRank graph expansion following the HippoRAG 2 approach to surface bridging associations. Optional idle-time automatic reorganization (sleep-time compute) and ONNX int8 embeddings are available via the [onnx] extra.

Memory lifecycle includes configurable reinforcement, decay, merging, and compression. Memories are never deleted due to decay and can be restored from archive.

⚙️ Key Details

Extension Modules (12 total, all disabled by default for base behavior)

Module Function
Fact extraction Extracts structured facts from input
QA pair replay Replays question-answer pairs
Temporal knowledge graph Builds time-aware knowledge graphs
User profiling Maintains user profiles
Fact version correction Corrects fact versions over time
Noise suppression Filters noisy inputs
WAL incremental persistence Write-ahead log for durability
Storage backend Pluggable storage
REST + SDK API and Python SDK access
Observability Metrics and monitoring
Hierarchical context Multi-level context management
Multi-user isolation Isolates memory per user

Presets (7 configurations)

  • Chat assistant
  • Knowledge base dynamic
  • Knowledge base static
  • Embodied robot
  • All off
  • Static retrieval · UNITED
  • Real model · semantic priority

Interfaces

  • Python SDK
  • REST API (FastAPI) with official client
  • MCP (agent-native, one-line mount)
  • Web configuration center (python -m sme.api then open browser)

Chinese-Friendly Features

  • Chinese 1-2 gram BM25 keyword channel enabled by default
  • Document clause import for legal/medical knowledge base scenarios

Explainable Retrieval

Every hit includes a breakdown of eight signals: semantic, importance, freshness, weight, decay, hit_count, recency, and region.

🚀 Availability

Installation: Zero-config offline operation. After installing core dependencies, a built-in hashing embedding runs the basic pipeline with no model downloads or API keys.

Core dependencies: numpy, httpx, fastapi, uvicorn, networkx, python-multipart, hnswlib (in [ann] extra). Install via pip install -r requirements.txt or pip install -e . (with pip install -e ".[ann]" for ANN acceleration; region scaling automatically enables ANN, falling back to exact scan otherwise).

Requirements: Python ≥ 3.10, Windows or Linux.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Benchmarked head-to-head against Mem0 and bare RAG
  • All 101 configuration items and 7 presets are fully toggleable
  • Performance figures: WAL group commit 2,557 writes/sec (1.79×), ONNX int8 batch embedding 7.4×, memory graph hot path O(E)→O(deg) measured 127–159×, hashing retrieval p50 ~4 ms at 2k items
  • Runs entirely offline with zero external dependencies for the base path

#AIMemory #RAG #LLM #Embeddings #OpenSource

Source: jack66g/spatial-memory-engine

item.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway Networking Requirements for Private MCP and REST APIs
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway Networking Requirements for Private MCP and REST APIs

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway now supports agents that call internal REST APIs and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, provided they meet specific network ownership and traffic inspection requirements.

🔍 Overview

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. The Gateway connects to private targets through an Amazon VPC Lattice resource gateway. This update clarifies where to place the resource gateway, who owns each network component, and the configuration decisions required for traffic to cross a central firewall in both directions.

🧩 How it works

The AgentCore Gateway reaches private targets through two private endpoint modes:

  • Managed mode: AgentCore creates the resource gateway for you. This fits environments where the Gateway account can own the subnets it runs in.
  • Self-managed mode: You create the resource gateway and give the target a resource configuration. As documented, this places it in subnets with direct access to the backend, fitting environments that do not require inspection between the Gateway and the tool.

In the pattern built and tested in the US East (N. Virginia) AWS Region (us-east-1), the network account owns the resource gateway and places it in subnets routed through AWS Transit Gateway. This ensures every request and reply between VPCs crosses the central firewall in an inspection VPC. The network team keeps ownership of every subnet, and traffic between the Gateway and private APIs and MCP servers crosses the central firewall in both directions.

⚙️ Key details

The architecture relies on specific VPC Lattice objects and sharing mechanisms:

  • Resource gateway: The Amazon VPC Lattice entry point into a VPC, utilizing elastic network interfaces (ENIs) in subnets you choose.
  • Resource configuration: A VPC Lattice object that names one backend (an internal load balancer or VPC endpoint DNS name and port) behind a resource gateway. This can be shared with other accounts through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).

Key ownership and traffic rules include:

  • A network account owns every VPC, subnet, and AWS Transit Gateway attachment, sharing application subnets through AWS RAM.
  • The Gateway account can own subnets that reach your tools.
  • The Gateway and application accounts build only in subnets shared to them through AWS RAM.
  • Tools are reachable on public endpoints if central inspection is not required for that specific flow, but in the documented pattern, every flow between VPCs crosses the central firewall.
  • The central firewall in the inspection VPC inspects the traffic between the Gateway and your private APIs and MCP servers.

🚀 Availability

The pattern was validated in a lab with three member accounts and a management account in AWS Organizations. The AWS CloudFormation templates, test scripts, test evidence, and reference material (address plan, full validation checks, troubleshooting, quotas) are available in the companion repository.

#AmazonBedrock #AgentCore #AI #Networking #MCP

Source: Connect Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs in a hub-and-spoke network with centralized inspection | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Context Engine launches AI skills for semantic code search and memory
item.description:
Context Engine launches AI skills for semantic code search and memory

🆕 Overview

Context Engine has launched a suite of AI agent skills designed to teach coding assistants how to utilize 30+ MCP tools for semantic search, symbol graph navigation, and memory. The tool provides semantic code search, memory, and symbol intelligence specifically for AI coding assistants.

🧩 How it works

The Context Engine MCP server indexes workspaces, allowing agents to call repo_search first for any question about the codebase before using standard commands like ls, find, Grep, or Read. Results from repo_search are verified source with exact line ranges, which agents are instructed to treat as already read.

The system includes specific tools for different coding tasks:

  • repo_search: Finds code by behavior, concept, error text, or identifier; supports multiple queries and narrowing by language, path, or type.
  • context_answer: Explains how or why something works across several files with citations.
  • symbol_graph: Shows definitions, callers, callees, importers, and references for specific symbols.
  • graph_query: Performs multi-hop impact analysis before making changes.
  • cross_repo_search: Identifies code that may exist in other indexed repositories.

For safety and efficiency, the system recommends fetching every involved symbol in one call before editing. For renames or signature changes, symbol_graph with query_type=references is used to get every site.

⚙️ Key details

The tool supports various development environments through specific installation and configuration methods:

  • Claude Code & Codex: Recommends pasting guidance into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md to reach subagents. Codex can install natively using its built-in skill installer, which pulls .codex/skills/context-engine/ into ~/.codex/skills/ automatically.
  • Cursor: Rules are included in .cursorrules at the workspace root, which Cursor picks up automatically if the file is present.
  • Terminal-based MCP clients: An MCP bridge allows connection without VS Code for clients like Claude Code or Codex.
  • Daemon Management: The system runs as a background daemon with a default file watch interval of 30 seconds. Users can authenticate, index codebases, and monitor changes. The daemon and MCP server share authentication via ~/.ctxce/auth.json, and logs are stored at ~/.context-engine/daemon.log.
  • Installation: Native installation is available from the public GitHub repo, which pulls the skill and auto-loads MCP tool guidance into the session.

🚀 Availability

Users can get a free account at dev.context-engine.ai.

#AI #CodingAssistants #MCP #SemanticSearch #DeveloperTools

Source: Context-Engine-AI/Context-Engine

item.title: Databricks Introduces CustomerLake Conversions for Agentic CDP
item.description:
Databricks Introduces CustomerLake Conversions for Agentic CDP

Databricks has introduced CustomerLake Conversions, a new capability within its Agentic CDP that connects first-party data and context directly to advertising activation and measurement. This feature is designed to help brands pursue more valuable conversions and improve return on ad spend (ROAS) while maintaining control over the data they share.

🧩 How it works

CustomerLake Conversions brings signal creation and activation to the environment where customer data and models already live. It integrates with CustomerLake, the Agentic CDP built natively in Databricks. The feature includes a dedicated Conversions tab within CustomerLake Campaign Agents, allowing marketers to:

  • Select conversion data
  • Configure destinations
  • Manage delivery within the Campaign Agents workflow

Paid media teams can use existing lifetime value models in Databricks to identify specific events, such as completed first purchases from customers likely to become repeat buyers, and configure the delivery of these purchase events to supported advertising platforms through CAPI (Conversions API).

💡 Use cases

The capability supports various business scenarios by leveraging specific data signals:

Business Context Data Signal Used Application
Retailer Predicted lifetime value Rapidly adjust lookalike targeting
B2B Company Qualified leads or closed won revenue Represent progress beyond a submitted form
Paid Media Team Existing lifetime value model Identify completed first purchases from customers likely to become repeat buyers

🔒 Data governance and agency collaboration

CustomerLake Conversions is designed so that customers own their data and stay in control. It provides a shared foundation for brands and agencies:

  • Agencies receive governed access to customer context in the lakehouse without copying or duplicating data.
  • The brand controls what is shared and with whom.
  • Agencies can utilize better data for their work.

🚀 Availability

CustomerLake Conversions will be accessible to all customers using Campaign Agents in CustomerLake when available. CustomerLake Campaign Agents help marketers build audiences in natural language, activate across channels, and power 1:1 personalized experiences.

📈 Strategic impact

The feature supports a shift away from traditional launch cycles, where a single campaign can take 6+ teams and 60+ days to launch. Instead, CustomerLake enables a continuous operating model where each customer interaction helps inform the next decision. As campaign insights flow back into Databricks, agents can help marketers and agencies recognize changes, recommend adjustments, and keep activation aligned with business goals.

#Databricks #CustomerData #MarketingTech #AdTech #CDP

Source: Introducing CustomerLake Conversions: Improve advertising performance with first-party customer context

item.title: Global Bank Evaluates Ten Agentic AI Platforms for Financial Services Workloads
item.description:
Global Bank Evaluates Ten Agentic AI Platforms for Financial Services Workloads

An industrial evaluation programme run by the innovation laboratory of a global bank has assessed ten agentic AI platforms across three financial-services workloads. This “bakeoff” evaluated systems spanning open-source frameworks, proprietary products, and hyperscaler ecosystems to address how enterprise platforms are currently procured and analyzed.

🔍 Overview

Agentic AI platforms—systems in which LLM agents plan, invoke tools, retain memory, and coordinate to change the state of enterprise systems—are being procured faster than they can be measured. While public agent benchmarks score models in fixed harnesses, enterprises buy integrated platforms where orchestration, memory, governance, and tooling layers dominate outcomes, largely relying on the strength of vendor demonstrations.

⚙️ Key details

A cross-functional panel assessed ten platforms on nine capability dimensions across three financial-services workloads:

  • Counterparty credit risk
  • Retrieval-augmented generation
  • Process automation

Analyses of the evaluation results showed that:

  • Scores separated the platforms into three tiers that are stable under alternative weightings.
  • Workload-specific strengths were surfaced that aggregate scores hid.
  • A secondary analysis revealed a halo effect, with Cronbach’s alpha = 0.98 across nominally distinct dimensions and rank correlations >= 0.93 with the total for eight of nine dimensions. This indicates that demonstration-based scoring measures presentation as much as capability.

💡 Why it matters

To turn enterprise platform evaluation from structured judgment into measurement, a new “gate-then-score” evaluation protocol is proposed. This protocol consists of:

  • Four layers: capability, execution reliability, governance gates, and business value
  • Trace-level reliability metrics estimated over repeated runs
  • An autonomy-readiness scale
  • A reproducibility protocol

#AIAgents #EnterpriseAI #FinTech #LLMOps

Source: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises

item.title: Hermes Memory UI Released for Agent Inspection
item.description:
Hermes Memory UI Released for Agent Inspection

The Read-only Hermes Agent plugin has been introduced for inspecting memory in the Hermes Dashboard and Hermes Desktop, providing a unified Python backend API alongside separate delivery artifacts.

🔍 Overview

  • Read-only Hermes Agent plugin for inspecting memory in Hermes Dashboard and Hermes Desktop.
  • The Dashboard and Desktop interfaces are separate delivery artifacts sharing only the profile-aware Python backend API.
  • The plugin is intentionally read-only and does not add, edit, replace, or remove memories.
  • Writes must go through Hermes’ memory and fact_store tools or provider classes to preserve validation, locking, mirroring, FTS, HRR vectors, and memory-bank maintenance.

🧩 Supported Memory Sources

Memory Source Description / Capabilities
Built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md) Agent notes, environment facts, project conventions, user profile, and preferences. Works always.
Session search Explicit read-only search over previous Hermes sessions via session_search tool, with optional source/type filters (CLI, Telegram, cron, Discord, web, API).
Holographic memory Local SQLite fact store at $HERMES_HOME/memory_store.db tracking facts, categories, trust scores, retrieval counters, and timestamps.
Mem0 memory Read-only Mem0 Platform memories via provider config, including scopes, scores, timestamps, and metadata.
Honcho memory Read-only Honcho workspace, host, peer, and provider configuration state with user/AI peer cards, representations, conclusions, and context search.
Mnemosyne memory Read-only local SQLite store inspection for episodes, facts, instructions, gists, and graph rows, with explicit recall and injected-context preview.
Hindsight memory Read-only/query-only Hindsight provider configuration state with explicit recall and reflect actions, and contents view for memory units and retained source documents.
ByteRover memory Read-only ByteRover CLI (brv) project status and registered locations, supporting explicit BM25 search and optional query/synthesis action.

⚙️ Key Technical Details

  • Built-in memory view works always, while external memory provider sections show only when configured.
  • Dashboard is a web plugin with its own manifest, tracked browser bundle, and stylesheet (dashboard/).
  • Desktop plugin (desktop/plugin.js) is a standalone, uncompiled ESM disk plugin importing only the Hermes Desktop SDK, React, and the JSX runtime without requiring an npm build.
  • The Desktop plugin registers the /memory full-page route, a Memory sidebar item, and an Open Memory command-palette action.
  • Desktop requests use the plugin-scoped, profile-aware ctx.rest client reaching the same /api/plugins/hermes-memory-ui/ backend used by Dashboard.
  • The regular plugin must be installed and present in plugins.enabled so Hermes mounts dashboard/plugin_api.py.

🚀 Installation and Availability

  • Default profile lives at ~/.hermes, while a named profile lives at ~/.hermes/profiles/<name> (use hermes -p <name> and set HERMES_HOME="$HOME/.hermes/profiles/<name>").
  • Install directly from GitHub: hermes plugins install xraysight/hermes-memory-ui --enable.
  • To enable the Hermes Desktop interface, copy the disk plugin to $HERMES_HOME/desktop-plugins/hermes-memory-ui/plugin.js.
  • Hermes Desktop inventories the UI separately under Settings → Plugins.
  • Update existing installation using hermes plugins update hermes-memory-ui.

#HermesAgent #AIPlugins #MemoryManagement #DeveloperTools

Source: xraysight/hermes-memory-ui

item.title: Meta's AI Agents Drive 3x Productivity in ML Technique Propagation
item.description:
Meta’s AI Agents Drive 3x Productivity in ML Technique Propagation

Meta’s Ranking Engineer Agent (REA) is an autonomous system that generates hypotheses, designs experiments, and proves new machine learning techniques on ads ranking models. Since March 2026, AI agents have handled over 60% of all technique propagation, showing 3x greater engineering productivity and a median 4x reduction in training compute across select combinations. This work is detailed in the paper ‘Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Template-Driven ML Development for Large Model Ecosystems.’

🔍 Overview

  • Meta’s ads recommendation system is powered by a large number of distinct ads ranking models.
  • A technique is anything that makes a ranking model better, such as architectural advancements, richer data representations, training optimizations, or efficiency improvements.
  • Meta started by standardizing model design and automating propagation, organizing models into a small set of reusable and composable building blocks.
  • Over the last 2 years, through standardization and automation, Meta has shipped 5,000+ technique-model combinations across their large, diverse fleet of models, reducing per-model engineering time by 92%.

🧩 How it works

  • Meta’s technique propagation system is built around three capabilities: Discovery, Generalization, and Adoption.
  • AI agents supercharge all these capabilities by taking on judgment-heavy, non-deterministic decision-making and bringing deep intelligence to the system.

⚙️ Key details

  • Early results show an estimated $45M+ in compute savings by the end of the year.
  • Meta’s template-driven approach reduced per-model engineering time by 92%, shipped 5,000+ technique-model combinations, improved offline model quality by 0.63% on average at neutral serving capacity, and delivered 0.86% cumulative online lift covering 70% of models by count.

💡 Why it matters

  • At Meta, the main challenge in improving user relevance and advertiser value has shifted from inventing new techniques to propagating them.
  • Fragmentation compounds quickly in large-scale ML systems, making it difficult to propagate high-impact ideas across the fleet.
  • Meta’s Standard Model Templates (SMT) approach standardizes model design into a curated set of reusable templates, reducing the complexity of shipping new ideas at scale.
  • This template-driven approach became the foundation for a broader ML development system, treating the landscape as a shared innovation surface.

#Meta #AIAgents #MLTechniques #AdsRanking #Productivity

Source: How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models Source: Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem

item.title: Monte Carlo releases official toolkit for AI coding agents
item.description:
Monte Carlo releases official toolkit for AI coding agents

Monte Carlo has released an official toolkit designed for AI coding agents. The toolkit bundles skills and plugins that bring data observability directly into development workflows, supporting integrations with tools like Claude Code and Cursor.

🧩 How it works

The release functions as a single mc-agent-toolkit plugin that works across supported editors. It bundles multiple capabilities, with each feature acting as a skill that can be used standalone or as part of a larger system. Skills are grouped by their specific job, falling into two main categories:

  • Orchestrated workflows: Sequence individual skills into guided multi-step flows.
  • Atomic skills: Can be invoked directly by name.

⚙️ Key details

The toolkit includes a variety of skills focused on data health, incident response, and agent observability:

  • Asset Health: Generates single-table health reports covering freshness, active alerts, monitor coverage, and upstream issues, intended to be run before building on a table.
  • Incident Response: Orchestrates the full incident lifecycle from triage to root cause and remediation.
    • Automated Triage: Scores and prioritizes active alerts, running deep troubleshooting on high-signal ones.
    • Analyze Root Cause: Investigates incidents using lineage tracing, ETL checks, query analysis, and data profiling.
    • Remediation: Proposes and executes fixes for data-quality alerts, assessing blast radius before acting.
  • Troubleshoot Agent Traces: Investigates AI-agent alerts and traces by kicking off the trace troubleshooting agent and guiding manual investigation.
  • Proactive Monitoring: Sequences coverage analysis, gap identification, and monitor creation into a guided flow.
    • Monitoring Advisor: Identifies coverage gaps and creates monitors for warehouse tables or AI agents, emitting monitors-as-code YAML.
    • Manage MaC: Handles the creation, editing, validation, and import of Monitors-as-Code YAML files against published JSON Schemas.
    • Tune Monitor: Recommends changes to sensitivity, segments, and schedules to reduce alert noise.
  • Account Analytics: Answers questions about the user’s Monte Carlo account and helps build dashboards.
  • Prevent: Acts as an edit-lifecycle safety net for dbt/SQL, auto-activating via hooks to surface blast radius and monitor gaps before edits.
  • Generate Validation Notebook: Creates targeted SQL validation queries for dbt PRs or local repository changes.
  • Storage Cost Analysis: Identifies storage waste (such as unread or zombie tables) and verifies cleanup safety using lineage.
  • Performance Diagnosis: Diagnoses slow pipelines and expensive queries across Airflow, dbt, Databricks, and other platforms.
  • Push Ingestion: Generates collection scripts to push metadata, lineage, or query logs to Monte Carlo from any data source.
  • Connection Auth Rules: Builds JSON rules for Monte Carlo connection types using live connector schemas.
  • Instrument Agent: Instruments Python AI agents for observability by detecting libraries, installing the Monte Carlo OpenTelemetry SDK, and setting up tracing.
  • Onboarding: Connects warehouses or BI tools (Tableau, Looker, Power BI) to Monte Carlo via the REST API v2 tools, choosing or provisioning deployments and emitting Terraform or scripts.

🚀 Availability

Users operating coding agents can install the mc-agent-toolkit plugin, which is recommended by Monte Carlo to bundle all skills, hooks, and related features. For those using Claude.ai (web or desktop) instead of a coding agent, Monte Carlo is available as a verified connector in the Claude directory, allowing direct installation.

item.title: QDA Automates Quantization Recipe Design for Large Language Models
item.description:
QDA Automates Quantization Recipe Design for Large Language Models

Researchers have introduced QDA, a system that uses an LLM agent to automatically design post-training quantization recipes for large language models, reducing the need for manual expert tuning.

🔍 Overview

  • Post-training quantization (PTQ) is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost.
  • The optimal quantization recipe varies across models and precisions, requiring experts to redesign it for each new model—a time-consuming and often sub-optimal process.
  • QDA automates this design by employing an LLM agent that iteratively refines quantization recipes over multiple rounds of building and evaluating candidates.

🧩 How it works

  • The agent explores candidate recipes through rounds of building and evaluation; more rounds yield better recipes.
  • To accelerate evaluation, QDA scores each candidate in minutes using output KL divergence from the original model on held-out reasoning traces, and validates promising candidates with long generations to detect failures such as repetition loops.
  • To accelerate building, QDA provides a library of public PTQ methods that are mutually compatible and compatible with new model architectures.

⚙️ Key details

  • Evaluated across four reasoning models, QDA improves accuracy over the strongest public recipe by:
    • 0.9 percentage points at W4A16
    • 1.4 percentage points at W4A8
    • 2.2 percentage points at W3A16
    • Using 64 GPU-hours per search.
  • On the 320B-parameter MoE model GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4 W4A4, QDA recovers 98.3% of the FP8 model’s accuracy, compared to 96.9% for the best vendor checkpoint.
  • All QDA checkpoints run on existing serving kernels with no inference overhead.

🚀 Availability

  • The library, evaluator, and harness will be released publicly.

💡 Why it matters

  • Automating quantization recipe design reduces expert effort and improves compression accuracy across diverse models and precision settings.
  • Faster evaluation and building enable practical deployment of quantized reasoning models at scale.

#Quantization #LLM #AIAgents #ModelCompression #PostTrainingQuantization

Source: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents Source: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models

item.title: RadixArk Releases DaisyRose-27B Model With RL Training on Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
item.description:
RadixArk Releases DaisyRose-27B Model With RL Training on Long-Horizon Agent Tasks

RadixArk has released DaisyRose-27B, its first model, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning using the Miles framework. The model was trained on 1,200 curated long-horizon agent tasks over 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs, achieving a Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 improvement from 5.6% to 12.0%.

🔍 Overview

  • First model release from RadixArk
  • Base: Qwen3.8-27B
  • Training method: Reinforcement learning via Miles (open-source RL framework)
  • Training scale: 1,200 tasks, sessions up to 1M tokens, 18 days, 144 H200 GPUs
  • License: Apache 2.0 checkpoints available

🧩 How It Works

Task Design

  • Tasks built in partnership with Eigent AI from a large pool covering machine learning, software engineering, science, and other fields
  • Thousands of candidates filtered to ~1,200 final tasks using three criteria:
    • Each task targets a mistake the original Qwen3.8-27B makes
    • Tasks redesigned around those mistakes, difficulty adjusted until solve rate falls in a useful learning range
    • Each task requires several interdependent steps: the agent must reason, plan, and execute across a long job
  • Each attempt runs up to 1.5 hours in a sandbox with >100 tool calls and >256K output tokens
  • Tasks must reward actually solving the problem; every task reviewed alongside model attempts; flawed tasks fixed or removed

Training Backend (Miles)

  • Fully asynchronous mode: agent keeps working while model learns, neither waits for the other
  • 128 H200s run inference on agent tasks; 16 H200s run the trainer
  • After each step, updated model deployed to the 128 inference GPUs
  • Internal training backend built for agent training: each step learns from a handful of very long sessions (up to 1M tokens) folded into multiple trajectories via harness summarization

Sandbox Service

  • Built on open-source AgentENV project (RadixArk contributes fixes)
  • Mid-September to mid-November: ~944,000 sandboxes run, up to 1,566 concurrent
  • Service scaled from 1 to 12 machines
  • 10 upgrades shipped, nearly all while training was running
  • 99% sandbox creation success across 9 weeks; >99.95% since late October

⚙️ Key Details

Benchmark Results

Benchmark Qwen3.8-27B DaisyRose-27B
Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 5.6% 12.0%
  • DaisyRose-27B scores higher than original Qwen3.8-27B on every benchmark evaluated
  • Largest gain on Terminal-Bench 4.1 (5.6% → 12.0%)
  • Gains also on reasoning, instruction following, and coding benchmarks
  • Scores use higher of BF16 and FP8 runs; difference <1 point where both evaluated

Model Architecture

  • Retains Qwen3.8-27B architecture, tokenizer, chat template, image understanding, and 256K-token context window
  • Longer training sessions use harness summarization to span multiple trajectories
  • Model thinks before answering by default; reasoning returned in reasoning_content, final answer in content

Training Efficiency

Metric RadixArk Backend Open-Source Trainer (Megatron)
Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) 37% 16%
Training cost reduction 57% less GPU time baseline
Throughput (tokens/sec across 144 GPUs) ~16,800 ~8,300
End-to-end speed 2× faster baseline
  • Stability: 63,000 GPU-hours over weeks; speed and efficiency held steady from first to last step
  • Larger gains on mixture-of-experts models: 6.2× on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, >10× on ~300B GLM-5.3-Flash

🚀 Availability

  • Checkpoints released under Apache 2.0
  • Recommended serving: SGLang with DSpark speculative decoding
  • SGLang cookbook provides launch configurations for different GPUs and checkpoint formats
  • Quickstart: start server with served model name DaisyRose-27B on port 30000, then send requests via OpenAI Python client

💡 Why It Matters

  • Demonstrates that carefully designed long-horizon agent tasks, an efficient asynchronous RL backend, and a robust sandbox service can jointly deliver large benchmark gains with substantially lower compute cost
  • 57% less GPU time for equivalent training via higher MFU (37% vs 16%)
  • 2× end-to-end throughput improvement
  • Sandbox infrastructure proved reliable at scale (99.95% success rate) with live upgrades during training
  • Gains generalize across benchmark categories and are especially pronounced on mixture-of-experts architectures

#RadixArk #DaisyRose #ReinforcementLearning #AIAgents #OpenSource #LLM

Source: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
