item.title: claude-tap Offers Local Tracing for AI Coding Agents
item.description:
claude-tap Offers Local Tracing for AI Coding Agents

claude-tap is a local proxy and trace viewer for AI coding agents, letting users inspect API traffic and agent context. Its workflow supports reviewing individual requests, comparing changes between turns, and exporting trace sessions as standalone HTML files.

🔍 What it captures

The viewer can show:

  • System prompts and conversation history
  • Tool schemas, tool calls, and tool results
  • Reconstructed streaming responses
  • Token usage
  • Diffs between adjacent requests

Users can run a CLI through claude-tap or listen to local app transcripts, then open an agent run and inspect its requests to see how context changes between turns. The viewer has light and dark modes.

🧩 Supported clients

The evidence lists support for these tools and clients:

  • Claude Code, Codex CLI, Codex App, and Gemini CLI
  • Grok Build CLI, DeepSeek Harness, Kimi CLI, and MiMo Code
  • OpenCode, OpenClaw, Pi, and Hermes Agent
  • Cursor CLI, Qoder CLI, and CodeBuddy CLI

🛠️ Traces and prompt snapshots

Each run writes a local trace session that can be exported as a self-contained HTML viewer for review or archiving. No hosted dashboard is required.

Phistory archives versioned system-prompt snapshots from agent CLIs, including Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, OpenCode, and Pi. It uses claude-tap’s capture-only prompt export to preserve raw HTTP trace evidence and create snapshots for comparison in a prompt diff viewer.

🔐 Data handling

Common authentication headers are replaced with *** before recording, without retaining credential prefixes. Upstream requests receive the original headers. The stated redaction does not cover request or response bodies, URLs, or diagnostic text.

#AIAgents #CodingAgents #DeveloperTools #APIDebugging

Source: liaohch3/claude-tap

item.title: Codex Router Connects Coding Clients to External Models
item.description:
Codex Router Connects Coding Clients to External Models

Codex Router lets users connect external models to Codex and other coding clients through one local router. It stores provider credentials locally and can share one installation across clients, while native GPT access remains available with a valid ChatGPT login.

🔍 How it works

The Control Center manages provider connections, model visibility, usage, and service health. Setup asks which providers to enable and uses private local prompts for credentials. Some providers require selecting models from their live catalog before models appear.

Client Integration described
Codex App and CLI Native and external models appear in the model picker; Linux support covers the CLI.
DeepSeek Harness Managed provider routes are available in its settings.
Gemini CLI Uses a managed endpoint, key, and default-model environment block.
Cursor Agent / Cursor App A local Agent launcher is available; App BYOK uses a separately keyed public HTTPS edge.
Claude Code Uses a separate claude-router launcher with the local Messages adapter.
OpenClaw Uses a managed Responses provider.
opencode, pi, omp, Command Code, Hermes Agent Provider configuration is published into the existing client.

Built-in integrations include Anthropic, Kimi, DeepSeek, xAI, Z.ai, Qwen, MiniMax, Meta, OpenRouter, GitHub Copilot, and others. Available models depend on the provider, region, account entitlement, and local selection.

⚙️ Features and requirements

  • Image, search, and subagent capabilities depend on the selected model route. Some features make additional provider requests and use additional quota.
  • The default Codex setup uses Codex App or CLI. Using another integration requires installing its supported client.
  • Node.js 22.19 or later is required; a maintained Node.js 24 LTS release is recommended.
  • Git is used for managed checkout installation, updates, and rollback.
  • The default compatibility-enabled source installation uses uv or Python 3.10 or later with venv. An explicit compatibility-layer opt-out skips Python installation and probes; source dependency setup follows the stored compatibility policy.
  • Homebrew installs the formula’s Python dependencies. On Windows, PowerShell must run in FullLanguage mode and policy must allow Add-Type.
  • Building the macOS desktop companion locally requires the full Xcode app.

🚀 Setup and operation

Homebrew provides the router and CLI; the source installer is used for the desktop companion. Use codex-router <command> for Codex maintenance commands and brew upgrade codex-router for updates.

After provider setup, run the doctor from the installed checkout and resolve any FAIL. On macOS or Linux, the command is ./bin/model-router codex doctor. Live inference tests run only when explicitly requested and consume quota from the selected provider.

Fully quit and reopen Codex, create a new task, and choose the intended model. Codex reads the router’s model catalog at startup. If a model is missing, check provider selection, authentication, and model visibility before reinstalling. Native GPT models also require a usable ChatGPT login.

Open Codex Router to access the Control Center. Closing its window normally leaves the tray running; use the tray or menu-bar entry to reopen it. macOS uses a native menu-bar host with an embedded Electron window, while Windows and Linux use an Electron window and tray.

#AI #CodingAgents #LLM #DeveloperTools

Source: duolahypercho/codex-router

item.title: Databricks introduces Skills for Genie One
item.description:
Databricks introduces Skills for Genie One

Databricks has introduced a new feature for Genie One called Skills, which adds a layer of control by defining specific workflow recipes that the agent can follow on demand to ensure consistent formats and outputs.

🧩 How it works

A skill is a durable, reusable asset that serves as a written record of how a team works, using plain language and the open Agent Skills format. Genie One leverages skills either when called directly by the user or when it decides a skill is relevant to the request.

  • Scope and Isolation: Guidance stays with the specific task rather than spilling into other work. Because Genie One only reads the skills it needs, keeping them specific and focused is advantageous for testing, fixing, and reusing them.
  • Chainable Assets: Small skills can be chained together; for example, updating a style guidelines skill once allows every other skill that uses it to pick up the change.
  • Judgment vs. Routines: While dashboards do the same thing every time, skills allow Genie One to make decisions, such as choosing the most important changes for leadership or following unusual results until they make sense.
  • Strict Rules: Skills define what must always appear, what to do when something is missing, and thresholds that decide what gets a closer look. For instance, a trading brief might always include a watch list even if nothing breached a threshold.

⚙️ Key details

Skills distinguish themselves from Genie Agents and Genie Ontology by focusing on the method rather than domain knowledge:

Component Function
Genie Ontology Tells Genie One what things mean.
Genie Agent Domain expert for one area (e.g., sales, finance, HR); knows metric definitions, tables, joins, and business rules.
Skill Recipe for a specific task: the steps, checklist, and output format.

For example, a sales pipeline Genie Agent knows the pipeline tables and stage definitions, while a “weekly forecast risk memo” skill instructs Genie One to compare current and previous pipeline data, flag slipped deals, and produce a one-page memo. The Genie Agent supplies domain knowledge, and the skill supplies the workflow.

💡 Why it matters

You can build a skill directly in Genie One by explaining your workflow in detail once, prompting the agent to interview you before writing the skill. Genie One draws on existing knowledge through Genie Ontology to focus questions on how you work rather than what your data means. Answering in plain language is enough for Genie One to write the skill. Once built, a skill can be published through Unity Gateway and used by any agent that supports MCP, including coding agents teams already use.

Consider using a skill when you find yourself explaining the same thing to Genie One more than once.

#Databricks #GenieOne #AISkills #MCP #WorkflowAutomation

Source: Teach Genie One your workflows: The ultimate guide for skills in Genie One

item.title: Eido 0.0.2 Adds Browser Automation and Localization to Native AI Workspace
item.description:
Eido 0.0.2 Adds Browser Automation and Localization to Native AI Workspace

Eido 0.0.2 is now available for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 13 or later. This update introduces browser and desktop automation capabilities, expanded localization options, and interface refinements for the native AI workspace built on Zed and the official pi agent.

🌐 Localization Updates

The interface now supports English and Simplified Chinese. Users can select Follow System, English, or 简体中文 at the top of the Settings menu. While common Eido controls and menus are localized, user content, code, model output, and tool identifiers remain unchanged.

🖥️ Interface Refinements

Several visual and usability improvements have been applied to the workspace:

  • Interface and conversation text default to 16px.
  • Ordinary completed tasks no longer leave a detached “Run finished” label; important status messages stay aligned with the input area.
  • Existing custom font preferences are preserved.
  • Users can drag the empty area in the top toolbar to move a non-fullscreen window on macOS.

🌐 Browser and Computer Use

The update introduces experimental features for extending tasks to websites and desktop applications. These capabilities are disabled by default and require separate DeepSeek service configuration. The release includes Chromium and its desktop driver. Users can also connect an existing Poki MCP installation to supported iPhone workflows, though Poki and device preparation are separate setup steps. Automation compatibility varies by website, application, and device.

To enable Computer Use, users must update global settings and grant specific macOS permissions:

  1. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security.
  2. Allow Eido under Accessibility and Screen & System Audio Recording (called Screen Recording on some macOS versions).
  3. Restart Eido.

These permissions allow input and window capture. Note that replacing a locally signed build can require re-enabling these permissions, and permission previously granted to a standalone Cua Driver does not apply to Eido.

🧩 Workflow and Configuration

The update retains pi’s public configuration and authentication interfaces while updating runtime adaptation. Key workflow features include:

  • Reference relevant files with @ and attach supporting material.
  • Continue earlier tasks with their saved context.
  • Review proposed file changes in the native editor before accepting them.
  • Search and fetch sources, inspect saved evidence, extract PDF/image text, and connect requirements with proposed changes and checks.

Model and thinking controls are located beside the composer in AI → pi Models & Credentials. Configuration and task history are stored outside the application bundle and are preserved during local updates.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Bundled Agent: pi 1.5.2
  • Signing Status: Locally signed; has not been notarized by Apple.
  • Release Assets: Include SHA-256 checksums, Eido source, and corresponding source for the native components.

item.title: Kody Updates Portable Cloud Platform for AI Agent Memory and Automations
item.description:
Kody Updates Portable Cloud Platform for AI Agent Memory and Automations

Kody has introduced new updates to its portable agents’ cloud, designed to manage the memory, keys, code, and automations of AI agents across Model Context Protocol (MCP) hosts. Built on Cloudflare Workers, this source-available platform supports both individuals and teams by providing account isolation and a flexible development environment.

🔍 Overview

Kody provides an MCP-first architecture intended to work across compatible AI agent hosts, with ChatGPT serving as a likely primary host target. Rather than functioning as a general-purpose agent harness, Kody focuses on enabling portability for an agent’s critical assets. Each account on the platform represents an isolated environment holding its own packages, jobs, credentials, memories, and related state. To maintain security, no account is given privileged status at runtime.

🧩 How it works

Instead of managing a large, static tool catalog, Kody prioritizes a compact MCP surface area designed around powerful flows. Key behaviors and request flows include:

  • Flow Preferences: The platform favors powerful search and Code Mode execute flows.
  • Request Ordering: OAuth requests are processed first, followed by MCP requests, and finally static assets.
  • Webhook Processing: Webhook ingress, including GET subscription challenges, is handled in the Worker fetch path before being routed to TanStack Start.
  • Web Application: The remaining website requests are routed through TanStack Start at packages/worker/start/http-entry.ts.
  • Client Assets: Assets are bundled into packages/worker/public/ and served via the ASSETS binding.

⚙️ Key details

The project utilizes an Nx monorepo structure following several epicflare starter conventions. Shared modules and worker roles are organized as follows:

Module / Package Path Description / Role
packages/shared (@kody-internal/shared) Shared modules used across the repository
packages/worker The origin app worker, with its entrypoint at packages/worker/src/index.ts
packages/platform-worker Sibling worker managing platform services
packages/runtime-worker Sibling worker managing runtime tasks
packages/jobs-worker Sibling worker managing automated jobs
packages/mock-servers/* Mock Workers for local testing and simulation

For contributors getting started with development, the local dev server runs on localhost:3742 by default. The command-line interface automatically selects the next free port if that one is occupied, and Wrangler manages both the local Cloudflare Workers runtime and the D1 database automatically. Developers and agents can refer to AGENTS.md for repository-specific guidelines, while docs/contributing/project-intent.md explains the core intent of the repository.

#Kody #ModelContextProtocol #CloudflareWorkers #AIAgents #Monorepo

Source: kody-hq/kody

item.title: LCU Decouples Codex Computer Use for Any Agent Harness
item.description:
LCU Decouples Codex Computer Use for Any Agent Harness

A new tool called LCU (Local Computer Use) has emerged, decoupling Codex’s original computer-use runtime from the Codex app to make it usable inside any agent harness, without requiring Codex authentication.

🔍 Overview

LCU exposes the original Codex computer-use runtime to local harnesses. To function, the official ChatGPT desktop app must remain installed locally; it supplies the runtime and instructions, while LCU handles setup and integration.

🧩 How it works

  • Desktop Apps: The system can read windows, click, type, and take screenshots.
  • Browsers: When enabled, it can read and control Chrome tabs through the official extension, subject to site approval.
  • Approvals: The first time an agent controls an app, the computer-use runtime asks the user to allow it.
  • Security: Only the user can answer the approval pane; the model cannot see, press, or fake the pane.

⚙️ Key details

  • Harness Adapters: Adapters are available for Pi, Codex CLI, and Claude Code, with experimental integrations for Oh My Pi, Hermes, DeepSeek Harness, and Junie.
  • Junie Limitations: With Junie, the agent cannot show LCU’s per-app prompt. Instead, it runs lcu apps allow <App> itself, and approval lasts permanently until the user revokes it.
  • High-Risk Apps: Browsers and password managers display warnings from the runtime. Apps that Computer Use outright refuses, such as Terminal and iTerm2, are declined. The app hosting the agent is never approved.
  • CLI Management: Users can review and change the approved app list from the terminal on macOS without opening the Codex app. Listing apps is free, but allowing or revoking requires the user to be at the machine.
Integration Details
Claude Code Requires version 2.1.287 or newer.
Claude App Register LCU through Claude Code (lcu setup --agent claude-code), not through Settings > Connectors.
Claude Code Mod The lcu-approve mod asks approval questions natively as a card in the app and an approval pane in the terminal.
Turn Limits In Claude Code, Computer Use normally ends when the turn that started it ends. A background subagent will be told “Computer Use is unavailable” unless an opt-in setting keeps it available for every turn of the session.

🚀 Availability

  • Mac Requirements: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac for Claude Code integration.
  • Setup: Setup involves two commands through the Claude Code plugin manager.
  • Command: Use /computer-use-apps to open an Approved apps panel in the terminal, displaying always-allowed apps with a Revoke option and an Allow field.

#LCU #ComputerUse #AIagents #Claude #DeveloperTools

Source: amontlabs/lcu

item.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 Released as Production-Ready Successor to Semantic Kernel
item.description:
Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 Released as Production-Ready Successor to Semantic Kernel

Semantic Kernel is now Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF), the enterprise-ready successor designed for building AI agents and multi-agent systems. MAF is now available at version 1.0 as a production-ready release, featuring stable APIs and a commitment to long-term support.

🧩 Core Capabilities

Microsoft Agent Framework is a model-agnostic SDK that empowers developers to build, orchestrate, and deploy AI agents. Key features include:

  • Multi-Agent Orchestration: Orchestrate complex workflows with collaborating specialist agents, suitable for both single assistants and fleets of specialized agents.
  • Model Support: Connect to any LLM with built-in support for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face, and NVidia.
  • Modular Design: Build modular AI agents with access to tools/plugins, memory, and planning capabilities.
  • Input Processing: Process text, vision, and audio inputs.
  • Local Execution: Run with Ollama, LMStudio, or ONNX.
  • Workflow Modeling: Model complex business processes with a structured workflow approach.

⚙️ Integration and Extensibility

The framework supports cross-runtime interoperability via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol and Model Context Protocol (MCP). Developers can extend agents using:

  • Native code functions
  • Prompt templates
  • OpenAPI specifications
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP)

It offers seamless integration with Azure AI Search, Elasticsearch, Chroma, and other data sources.

🚀 Platform Requirements

Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 is built for observability, security, and stable APIs, with the following platform support:

Language/Platform Version Requirement
Python 3.11 through 3.14
.NET .NET 10.0+
Java JDK 17+
Operating Systems Windows, macOS, Linux

#MicrosoftAgentFramework #SemanticKernel #AIagents #MultiAgentSystems #LLM

item.title: MoEngage and Amazon Build Agentic Customer Engagement Platform with MCP
item.description:
MoEngage and Amazon Build Agentic Customer Engagement Platform with MCP

MoEngage, an agentic customer engagement platform used by more than 1,350 consumer brands, has built a new layer of AI agents called Merlin AI that allows marketing and product teams to draft, analyze, and adjust campaigns through a single conversation. The system is built on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, leveraging the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to provide secure, tenant-scoped access to live platform data.

🔍 Overview

The traditional customer engagement workflow requires teams to navigate multiple tools—analytics dashboards, content libraries, and campaign builders—across channels like email, push, SMS, and WhatsApp. MoEngage addressed this by creating a third layer of software interaction where users describe an outcome in plain language and an agent executes the steps across the platform. This approach treats the platform’s existing API capabilities as tools for agents to call, reducing the need to switch between separate interfaces.

🧩 How it works

Merlin AI operates using a foundation of Amazon Bedrock for reasoning and generation, the AgentCore runtime for hosting, and MCP for standardized data access. The system utilizes Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 models for tool-call planning and content generation. The architecture is designed to keep each tenant’s data isolated while giving agents secure access to segments, campaign history, and content libraries.

⚙️ Key details

Merlin AI Studio places purpose-built agents at specific points in the marketing workflow:

  • Copywriter: Generates personalized push and transactional copy consistent with brand voice.
  • Designer: Produces marketing banners or images from text descriptions.
  • Segment Assist: Converts plain-language audience descriptions into specific attribute filters (e.g., users who abandoned a cart in the last two hours).
  • Jinja Assist: Translates natural language into working Jinja and Liquid markup for dynamic content.
  • In-app Template Builder: Creates responsive, accessible HTML templates for in-app messages, including gamified formats and surveys.
  • Flow Assist: Transforms high-level ideas into ready-to-deploy customer journeys by interpreting requests, proposing paths, and refining structures with historical data.

Conversational agents operate across campaigns, analytics, segments, and flows, allowing teams to manage complex interactions through a single dialogue.

💡 Why it matters

This development represents a shift in software platforms from user interfaces for business users and APIs for engineering teams to an agentic layer. A customer of MoEngage, Glance, reported a 38% uplift in push notification click-through rates as a result of using these AI agents. The architecture allows marketing teams to spend less time navigating tools and more time making decisions.

🏢 Legacy Modernization Context

In parallel developments, the evidence describes a methodology for transforming legacy mainframe Assembler applications into Java Spring Boot services on AWS. This process uses Amazon Bedrock and Kiro IDE for AI-assisted code analysis and business rule extraction, followed by AWS Transform for automated COBOL-to-Java conversion. The multi-stage approach converts Assembler to COBOL as an intermediate step to preserve business logic before final modernization, addressing the challenge of retiring critical code that few experts can read.

#MoEngage #AmazonBedrock #MCP #AIAgents #LegacyModernization

Source: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services Source: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform | Amazon Web Services

item.title: OpenInference Traces AI Agents Using OpenTelemetry Standard
item.description:
OpenInference Traces AI Agents Using OpenTelemetry Standard

OpenInference is a specification that builds on OpenTelemetry to trace AI agents, including their LLM calls, tool use, retrieval, and reasoning steps. It defines how AI applications are recorded as OpenTelemetry traces, ensuring that instrumentation follows a consistent standard regardless of the framework or language used.

🔍 Overview

  • The specification defines which span kinds mark LLM calls, agents, tools, retrievers, and embeddings.
  • It specifies which attributes hold inputs, outputs, token counts, and metadata.
  • Instrumentation follows the specification so that traces read the same whichever framework or language produced them.

🧩 How it works

  • OpenInference builds on OpenTelemetry to capture the execution flow of AI agents.
  • Instrumentation libraries automatically trace popular model providers and agent frameworks.
  • The system records specific steps such as LLM calls, tool use, retrieval, and reasoning.

item.title: Perplexity hits $1B revenue; Qwen4-Max and OpenAI evals released
item.description:
Perplexity hits $1B revenue; Qwen4-Max and OpenAI evals released

Perplexity has crossed a $1B annual revenue run rate, according to CEO Aravind Srinivas, while Alibaba’s Qwen4-Max preview moved to a shipping model and OpenAI granted external partners access to its internal systems for evaluation.

🔍 Overview

  • Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas told Semafor that the company crossed a $1B annual revenue run rate.
  • The Information previously reported Perplexity was under $250M at the start of the year and over $750M by August.
  • The growth was partly driven by its product, Computer.
  • At typical agent lab multiples, this revenue level suggests a valuation of roughly $30-50B for Perplexity.
  • This performance builds on a $20B funding round in September 2025.

🧩 How it works

  • Perplexity Features:
    • September’s Automations allow the system to pick up recurring tasks.
    • November’s Teammates handle ongoing jobs.
    • Computer runs fully locally on supported Macs.
    • The Monitor API watches a topic or page and triggers a webhook when relevant changes occur.
  • Qwen4-Max Specifications:
    • Total parameter count is 2.4T, with 71B active per token (a 25% reduction).
    • Accepts images and text with a 1M-token context window.
    • Smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are planned for release.
  • OpenAI Evaluation Program:
    • Apollo, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire have internal access to OpenAI models and systems.
    • Apollo places six evaluators onsite for four months.
    • METR reviews OpenAI’s largest RL run with access to transcripts, monitor records, and checkpoint snapshots.
    • Transluce conducts a six-week audit of post-training alignment evals, with a fuller follow-up in early 2027.
    • Goodfire embeds interpretability researchers to monitor training runs.

⚙️ Key details

  • Qwen4-Max Performance:

    • Scored 43 on the Intelligence Index at the highest reasoning setting, up from 34.
    • Average cost fell from $10.02 to $3.27 per task.
    • Alibaba cut output pricing from $6 to $4.50 per million tokens; the model generated about 39% fewer tokens.
    • On Arena, it ranks #14 overall and is the top Chinese model, with +7.5% net over 14.7k sessions.
    • Placed #6 in Code Arena WebDev at 1750, up 74 points from its predecessor.
    • Placed #6 in Image-to-WebDev, just above Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol.
    • Ranked #11 overall on Vals, with gains in coding and finance.
    • On HLAB, it gets 95.7% of checklist items right but passes only 21.3% of tasks, with output tokens rising 3.6x.
    • Roboflow notes it is underwhelming on its VLM benchmark compared to Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic.
    • At high reasoning effort, it is ~4.5x faster and ~68% cheaper per image than Qwen3.8-Max.

  • Competitor Benchmark:

    • Kimi K3.1 Pro cost $3.68 per index task and scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, compared to Qwen’s 48%.

💡 Why it matters

  • Perplexity’s revenue milestone qualifies it for the “>$10B fundraise” rule, marking a significant valuation increase.
  • The new Perplexity research lab has access to 10,000+ GPUs and plans to publish papers, data, models, and code.
  • OpenAI’s decision to grant internal access to independent evaluators represents a structured approach to external safety and alignment auditing.

#Perplexity #Qwen4-Max #OpenAI #AIEvaluations #Revenue

item.title: PineScript Expert Agent and ReAgent Archival Update
item.description:
PineScript Expert Agent and ReAgent Archival Update

Two recent developments in the AI and reinforcement learning space have been noted: the release of a RAG-based Pine Script expert agent built with Pydantic AI, and the official archival of the ReAgent reinforcement learning platform in favor of Pearl.

📗 PineScript Expert Agent

PineScript Expert is a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agent developed using Pydantic AI that serves as an expert on Pine Script v6, the programming language used for custom indicators and strategies on TradingView. The system leverages vector search technology and large language models to provide accurate, context-aware answers and generate working code examples.

Key Features

  • Comprehensive Knowledge: Accesses the entire Pine Script v6 documentation through natural language queries using a custom crawler.
  • Code Generation: Creates custom indicators and strategies based on specific user requirements.
  • Interfaces: Offers a web-based UI built with Streamlit (with persistent chat history) and an interactive command-line interface.
  • Multi-Provider Support: Utilizes either OpenAI or OpenRouter models as the LLM backend.
  • Vector Search: Uses pgvector for efficient semantic retrieval of relevant documentation.

Technical Requirements

  • Python 3.11+
  • PostgreSQL with pgvector extension (configured to run on port 54322)
  • OpenAI API key (required for embeddings and default LLM)
  • OpenRouter API key (optional, for alternative LLM providers)
  • Docker (optional, for running PostgreSQL with pgvector)

🛑 ReAgent Archival

ReAgent, an open-source end-to-end platform for applied reinforcement learning developed and used at Facebook, is officially archived and no longer maintained. For latest support on production-ready reinforcement learning, the developers direct users to Pearl, a production-ready RL AI Agent Library developed by the Applied Reinforcement Learning team at Meta.

Platform Details

  • Architecture: Built in Python, using PyTorch for modeling/training and TorchScript for model serving.
  • Use Case: Designed for large-scale, distributed recommendation/optimization tasks where a simulator is not accessible, relying on offline training on batches of data.
  • Methodology: Utilizes off-policy algorithms because policies update slowly and in batches.
  • Key Tools: Includes counterfactual policy evaluation (CPE) to test new policies without deployment, a Domain Analysis Tool to assess suitability for batch RL, and Behavior Cloning to bootstrap learning safely.
  • License: Released under a BSD 3-Clause license.

#PineScript #ReinforcementLearning #PydanticAI #TradingView #Meta #RL

item.title: Rust-Powered Multi-Protocol Download Manager Features Dynamic Acceleration and AI Agent Integration
item.description:
Rust-Powered Multi-Protocol Download Manager Features Dynamic Acceleration and AI Agent Integration

A new open-source download manager powered by Rust and the Tokio engine has been released as a free alternative to IDM. The tool features dynamic download acceleration with adaptive segmentation and is designed to be AI-agent ready through a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

🔍 Overview

The manager is a local-first, multi-protocol solution that requires no account for local downloads and contains zero advertisements. It uses a shared Rust + Tokio engine that remains independent of the UI and Foreign Function Interface (FFI), allowing it to power various client types from a single core.

  • Multi-protocol support: Handles HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, BitTorrent (including magnet links), eD2K, and streaming via HLS and DASH.
  • Cross-platform clients: Native GPUI desktop apps, Kotlin Android and SwiftUI iOS apps, a React Web UI, and a standalone CLI.
  • Browser integration: Includes a 3-layer interception engine for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, supplemented by a userscript.

🧩 How it works

The engine implements dynamic download acceleration by splitting segments at runtime. If a segment is performing poorly, idle workers utilize a “slow-segment rescue” feature to take over the task. For persistence, the manager uses SQLite with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) by default to store resumable states, while server deployments have the option to use PostgreSQL.

Protocol Capabilities
BitTorrent Supports DHT, UPnP, and magnet links
eD2K / eMule Server and Kad DHT source finding with MD4 verification
HLS / DASH Streaming media sniffing and AES-decryption support
Automation RSS subscriptions, scheduled queues, and JavaScript plugins

⚙️ Key details

The software includes professional-grade management tools such as named queues, global token-bucket rate limiting, and connection diagnostics. For developers and power users, it provides several integration paths:

  • AI Readiness: A built-in MCP server with 12 tools allows Claude, Cursor, and other AI clients to manage downloads.
  • Remote Management: Optional FluxCloud device collaboration for settings sync, remote task management, and LAN device pairing.
  • API Support: Offers REST/OpenAPI and aria2-compatible JSON-RPC interfaces.
  • Privacy: Anonymous installation and daily-active statistics can be disabled via settings and do not collect task-specific information.

🚀 Availability

The manager is available across multiple platforms including Windows, macOS, Linux, NAS, and Android. The desktop version includes a system tray service to keep downloads active after the main UI is closed. Users can choose between native GPUI interfaces or a React-based web management console, both supporting light, dark, and custom themes.

#Rust #OpenSource #AIagents #MCP #DownloadManager

Source: zerx-lab/FluxDown

item.title: Sovereign Core Unveils Open-Source AI-Driven Simulation Engine
item.description:
Sovereign Core Unveils Open-Source AI-Driven Simulation Engine

This week, Sovereign Core announced a new open‑source simulation platform that integrates a robust AI orchestration layer, a fault‑tolerant state grid, and a responsive command interface.

🔍 Overview

  • Provides a complete backend runtime, AI orchestration layer, and a responsive command interface for sovereign simulation environments.
  • Suitable for supply‑chain resilience, crisis response protocol testing, and synthetic training grounds for autonomous agents.
  • Delivers the structural integrity of a military‑grade simulation while remaining an open‑source framework.

🧩 How It Works

  • Fault‑tolerant grid distributes state, enabling operators to zoom from a macro‑level theater of operations down to individual asset behaviors without latency penalties.
  • Temporal event bus decouples simulation speed from rendering speed, allowing real‑time navigation of past, present, and speculative future states as layers.
  • The command interface is built on a reactive component architecture that consumes these layers without blocking input, ensuring fluid interaction even with tens of thousands of active entities.
  • A custom gleam‑engine propagates state updates in sub‑millisecond time across all connected clients.
  • A built‑in translation and localization pipeline supports English, Japanese, German, and Arabic, including a community‑driven framework for additional locales.
  • Natural‑language commands (voice or text) are parsed and executed in real time.
  • The UI adapts not only to screen size but also to operator role: logistics officers and tactical directors interact with different but synchronized control sets.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Cortical adapter treats the simulation as a sensorium for intelligent agents; the same APIs can be used by both human and AI operators.
  • The adapter allows pluggable backends—from lightweight heuristics to large language models running on private infrastructure.
  • An event‑sourced, lock‑free concurrency model underpins the simulation, making it a deterministic state machine that can be checkpointed, rewound, or forked.
  • Features speculative “what‑if” branches, scenario replay, and distributed computation across clusters.
  • The engine is written in a memory‑safe language with zero‑cost abstractions, enabling it to run on anything from a developer laptop to a dedicated server farm.
  • A built‑in health circuit monitors subsystems; upon failure (network partition, node crash, or data corruption), it automatically re‑routes and re‑establishes state, with structured, encrypted logs available for post‑mortem analysis.

🚀 Availability

  • The initial deployment package contains:
    • Core simulation runtime
    • Sample neural command agent
    • Bilingual (English / Japanese) interface template

💡 Why It Matters

  • The platform’s architecture allows for latency‑free, multi‑scale simulation, essential for realistic training and operational planning.
  • By integrating AI through a cortical adapter, future systems can expand to autonomous decision‑making within the same simulation environment.

item.title: Understanding AI Coordination Patterns
item.description:
Understanding AI Coordination Patterns

AI coordination patterns are crucial for effective multi-agent systems. When early implementations fall short, the cause is rarely the model.

🔍 Overview

  • Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem.
  • ~88% of AI pilots never reach production.
  • Two models can perform worse collaborating than either alone when coordination overhead exceeds the benefit.
  • Teams are adding complexity faster than they build understanding.
  • Ten steps that are each 95 percent reliable deliver only 59.9 percent end-to-end reliability.
  • 20 steps deliver 35.8 percent.
  • Each dependent handoff multiplies risk.

🧩 How it works

Coordination patterns fall into two tiers, based on who controls the flow.

Tier 1: Patterns (deterministic control flow)

  • Sequential Pipeline: Orchestration patterns that implement linear execution where each node’s output feeds into the next node (A -> B -> C) supporting ordered processing with predictable execution timing.
  • Conditional Workflow: Logic-based edges select the next node by condition, so the workflow can branch and send each case down a different path.
  • Conditional Router: A classification step examines the input and directs it to the appropriate processing path. Only one path is executed per request.
  • Parallel Workflow: A task splits into independent subtasks that run simultaneously across handlers, each on its own data. A fan-in step combines the results when all handlers complete, and a failure in one path retries only that path.

Tier 2: Autonomous patterns (LLM-determined control flow)

  • In autonomous patterns, control flow is determined at runtime by the AI model itself, not predefined by developers.
  • Plan-based orchestration: In plan-based orchestration, a single orchestrator agent acts as a project manager.
    • The orchestrator maintains an explicit task plan with assignments and dependencies, sees all context while each worker receives only its slice, distributes work dynamically against the current plan, and monitors progress centrally.
    • Key design choice is that the workers are stateless and independent. If one fails, it doesn’t contaminate others.
    • The orchestrator retries only the failed worker, not the entire workflow.
  • Handoff pattern: Agents operate with limited, local knowledge and coordinate through peer-to-peer delegation.
    • Each makes local decisions about when and to whom to transfer control, based on the task and the agents it knows.
    • Control passes with state: each transfer carries validated task state, the evidence behind it, and any unresolved questions, so the receiving agent continues rather than reinterpreting a summary.

💡 Why it matters

  • The practical default is to start with Tier 1 and move a task to Tier 2 only when its subtasks emerge during the work.

#AICoordination #MultiAgentSystems #AIAgents #DistributedSystems

Source: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base adds tabular search for agentic retrieval
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base adds tabular search for agentic retrieval

Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base adds tabular search, enabling agentic retrieval to answer analytical questions from tables combined with related documents.

🔍 Overview

  • Tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base lets agents get answers from tables through agentic retrieval.
  • When a question needs data from CSV, XLSX, or XLS files, tabular search looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row in one or more tables or sheets.
  • It combines results with facts from related documents to answer analytical questions that take several steps.
  • Example: A finance team closing the quarter asks “Which departments must write variance commentary?” No single file has the answer; it depends on the variance policy’s threshold, the quarter-close memo’s budget revisions, and math over every department in the profit and loss (P&L) workbook.
  • Most teams keep narratives and data in the same place; for example, a Microsoft SharePoint site holds workbooks next to policies, and an Amazon S3 bucket holds CSV exports next to PDFs.

🔧 How It Works

  • Tabular search is part of the agentic retrieval flow; there’s nothing to turn on.
  • When a question needs the data in a table, the request moves through these stages:
    • Retrieve: Passages come back, including passages from a table file.
    • Plan: The agent uses the question and table structure to determine whether to run code over one or more retrieved tables.
    • Stage: Tabular search copies the original file into an isolated sandbox with no network access.
    • Compute: Model-written code runs over the whole table or sheet.
    • Return: The agent gets back only what the code prints, such as totals or matching rows.
    • Answer: The agent answers from the results and the passages, with citations.
  • Tabular search starts when retrieved passages come from a CSV, XLSX, or XLS file and the question needs a calculation across rows or a lookup of specific values.
  • The Retrieve API keeps returning passages and doesn’t run code.
  • Tables lose information when split into passages, in ways that depend on the table’s shape:
    • Long tables: A table with thousands of rows spans many passages, and retrieval returns only the few that best match the question. An answer built from them uses a handful of rows, so a total, a comparison, or a threshold check can be incomplete.
    • Wide tables: In a table with hundreds of columns, one row can hold more text than a passage or a search model takes in at once. As a result, values in later columns are harder to match.
    • Long passages from wide tables can also match many unrelated questions and push more relevant passages out of the results.
  • Retrieval also has to match a question to the right table; questions use business terms such as “controllable spend,” but tables hold cost center codes, account names, and numbers.
  • A draft and a final workbook look almost the same to search.
  • The rule that gives the numbers meaning is often in a separate document, such as a policy.
  • Tabular search therefore splits the work: retrieval only has to return one passage from the right table file, and code then reads the whole table.
  • Because retrieval still has to find that file first, naming the file in your question helps.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Tabular search is built for questions that need calculations or lookups over the table files it retrieves.
  • Running code adds at least one more agent turn, so answers that use table data take longer than text-only answers.
  • Governed metrics, recurring dashboards, warehouse-scale joins, and reporting controls still belong in business intelligence (BI) tools.
  • Tabular search works on table files stored next to your documents, and you don’t define a schema.
  • In this solution, an Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base stores your CSV and Excel files together with related documents.
  • Then an agent running Amazon Bedrock’s Claude 3 reads the files and decides whether to run code over them to answer specific questions.
  • The trace shows which files the code was run over.
  • To see what tabular search can do, build a knowledge base from a set of sample finance files, then run a question that needs a calculation across rows and check the trace to see which file the code read.
  • The knowledge base automatically converts the XLSX workbook to a CSV format for analysis.
  • The example question “Which departments must write variance commentary?” needs data from three sources: the variance threshold from the policy, the list of departments and their variances from the workbook, and the list of revised budgets from the memo.
  • Sending an AgenticRetrieveStream request with that prompt returns the full answer and citations to the sources.
  • The trace shows which passages the search model found and which of those passages the agent used to build the answer; for tabular search, it also shows which file the code was run over.
  • In the trace, look for a passage that says: “Based on the provided variance data, the following departments exceed the 5% threshold and require variance commentary: Sales (6.3%), Engineering (6.1%), and Operations (5.5%).”
  • The source for that passage isn’t the P&L workbook; it’s a file that begins with “thought” and ends with “.csv”.
  • To see what that file contains, copy the “sourceUri” value, including the “s3://” prefix, into the URL bar of a browser logged into AWS, such as the AWS Management Console.
  • When you open the URL, you see the result of the calculation over the P&L workbook.
  • The file contains the question, the revised budgets from the memo, and the calculated variances.
  • Looking back at the trace, the agent used only two passages from the original files: the list of revised budgets from the memo and the definition of the variance threshold from the policy.
  • It didn’t refer to the workbook at all because it used the computed results instead.

💡 Why It Matters

  • With retrieval instructions in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, you can customize answers per tenant.
  • The same product and policy documents often serve several audiences, such as customers in different regions or internal teams, and each audience needs its own answer.
  • You set the voice, format, retrieval guidance, and answer policy that agentic retrieval applies to each request.
  • Before this feature, you couldn’t set the answer style, so agentic retrieval could use a different style from one request to the next.
  • For a fixed voice or structured output, you had to turn off response generation, call a model yourself, and maintain the prompt in every application.
  • Now you write that guidance once, as a managed, versioned Amazon Bedrock resource, and each request references it.
  • When you change an instruction, you can pin a version so that each application switches to the new version when you’re ready.
  • AnyCompany Smart Home, a fictitious company that sells a home controller and room sensors in three sales regions, serves as an example; its customer assistant serves all three regions, and its support, field sales, and legal teams use internal assistants built on the same documents; AnyCompany defines each region and internal team as a tenant, and each needs a different answer; a customer in Sales Region Central needs Spanish with day/month/year dates, and a support agent needs a short ticket note; to keep the example compact, every tenant queries one knowledge base, however agentic retrieval can search up to five knowledge bases in a single request, and the tenant’s instruction applies to all of them.
  • Retrieval instructions change how the assistant answers, but they aren’t an authorization or data-isolation boundary; use metadata filters or separate knowledge bases to control what each tenant can retrieve.
  • Tenants that share documents still differ in language, date and money conventions, voice, and which policy values they can quote.
  • A retrieval instruction has four fields for these differences: persona, who the assistant is including identity, tone, and language; answerFormat, how the answer is structured including how it cites sources; retrievalGuidance, how the agent interprets the question and what it prioritizes when it searches; answerPolicy, whether and how to answer, including questions outside scope.
  • The persona, answerFormat, and answerPolicy fields apply only when generateResponse is true, which is the default, and retrievalGuidance applies either way.
  • An instruction belongs to your AWS account and AWS Region, not to a knowledge base, and goes through these stages: Create (CreateRetrievalInstruction returns HTTP 202), Review (Amazon Bedrock reviews the instruction’s fields asynchronously, and you poll for the result), Activate (a passing review makes the instruction ACTIVE, and DRAFT points to its current content), Version (CreateRetrievalInstructionVersion saves an immutable numbered version), Apply (a request names the instruction and, optionally, a version, which defaults to DRAFT), Report (the first Planning trace event includes appliedInstruction).
  • Instructions set voice, format, conventions, and policy wording; they don’t limit which documents the agent can retrieve, and they don’t choose the tenant’s own values, which come from naming the tenant in the request; use metadata filters or separate knowledge bases to limit what each tenant can retrieve, and each tenant gets its own instruction and metadata filter; your backend chooses both from the authenticated tenant, so one shared knowledge base can serve every tenant; a request can query a shared global knowledge base and the tenant’s own knowledge base together, each with its own filter.

#AmazonBedrock #TabularSearch #AgenticRetrieval

Source: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base | Amazon Web Services Source: Customize answers per tenant in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Browser Use releases Pi Mono-based web agent with cloud browser support
item.description:
Browser Use releases Pi Mono-based web agent with cloud browser support

Browser Use has announced a new AI web agent built on Pi Mono, described as a tiny TypeScript web agent that hill climbed on real browser evaluations. The agent writes JavaScript, controls Chrome, and builds the helpers it needs dynamically. It uses Pi Mono plus a persistent V8 REPL and raw CDP to enable programmability with sessions, saved logins, streaming and typed results. The implementation is provided as a single SDK that can be integrated into applications via npm install @browser_use/pi, pnpm add @browser_use/pi, or bun add @browser_use/pi. Developers need Node 22.19+ or Bun 1.3.14+ (with Bun requiring Node for the V8 worker). The system uses Browser Use Cloud, so no local Chrome installation is needed, and supports upstream Pi’s model catalog and transports with custom providers, sessions with follow-ups and saved logins, persistent workspaces, and cloud browsers or user-owned Chrome. An ultrafast mode minimizes waits after actions, and the platform provides interaction highlights, recordings, and GIF exports. JavaScript runs in a separate worker with filesystem and network access, while anonymous run counters are enabled by default but can be disabled through telemetry settings or the DO_NOT_TRACK environment variable.

#AIagents #TypeScript #webautomation #PiMono #BrowserAutomation

Source: browser-use/browser-use-pi

item.title: E2B Desktop Sandbox Enables Secure AI-Driven Computer Use
item.description:
E2B Desktop Sandbox Enables Secure AI-Driven Computer Use

E2B Desktop Sandbox introduces an open‑source secure virtual desktop that can be connected to any large language model for safe computer interactions.

🔍 Overview

  • E2B Desktop Sandbox is an open source secure virtual desktop ready for Computer Use.
  • It offers a desktop graphical environment that can connect to any LLM for secure computer use.
  • The sandbox is built on top of E2B Sandbox.

🧩 How it Works

  • Each sandbox is isolated from the others and can be customized with any dependencies you want.
  • The sandbox template and example code are maintained in this repository.
  • SDK sources for JavaScript and Python are now in the E2B monorepo under packages/desktop-js and packages/desktop-python.
  • Authentication uses an auto‑generated key; you can retrieve the authentication key.
  • Set the environment variable E2B_API_KEY with your API key.
  • Only one stream is allowed at a time:
    • Stop the current stream before starting another.
    • An error is raised if the desired application is not open.
    • The stream closes automatically when the application closes.
    • Multiple streams cannot run simultaneously.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Powered by E2B.
  • The OpenAI Computer Use Agent uses E2B’s Desktop Sandbox.
  • The system runs as a Next.js app.
  • Computer use is achieved with 100% open source LLMs.

🚀 Availability

  • Sign up at E2B to receive an API key.

💡 Why it Matters

E2B Desktop Sandbox provides a secure, isolated environment for AI agents to interact with a computer system, ensuring safe and controlled usage across diverse applications.

#E2B #LLM #OpenSource #AIAgents #SecureCompute

Source: e2b-dev/desktop

item.title: Google Maps adds AI trip planning and appointment finding via Ask Maps
item.description:
Google Maps adds AI trip planning and appointment finding via Ask Maps

Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries and provide real-time details about each stop. The update is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app.

🧩 How it works

The AI-powered Ask Maps feature can suggest stops for your next trip while providing real-time details about each location. Users can plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days. For example, Google states that you can use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping or create a schedule for a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. From there, Ask Maps generates a day-by-day schedule with a list of stops, showing your route and numbered pins for each location on the map.

⚙️ Key details

  • You can share the itinerary with friends or family members.
  • You can export the itinerary to Google Docs on desktop.
  • You can ask Maps to show your trip schedule before you leave or select the “itinerary” badge in your chat history.
  • Google Maps displays real-time information about traffic and a location’s hours alongside directions.
  • The “know before you go” details include parking, car charging, weather conditions, potential delays, and tolls during your trip.
  • Ask Maps can find specific beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments and call the locations for you.
  • You can find saved places on your list by asking queries like, “Which spots on saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”

🚀 Availability

Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Trip-planning and saved list search are rolling out to the more than 200 countries where Ask Maps is available. The “know before you go” tips and appointment-finding features are launching in the US to start.

#GoogleMaps #AskMaps #AItourism #TripPlanning #Google

item.title: Grafana Releases Agent Observability SDKs and Plugins
item.description:
Grafana Releases Agent Observability SDKs and Plugins

Grafana has released open‑source SDKs and plugins that let developers instrument and monitor their coding agents in Grafana Cloud.

🔍 Overview

  • Grafana Agent Observability monitors agents you build and coding agents.
  • The repo provides open‑source SDKs and plugins that send telemetry to it.
  • Capture sessions from coding agents like Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Vibe, experimental Kiro CLI, and others.

🧩 How it Works

  • Install the agento11y plugin for supported coding agents (except Hermes). Hermes has a separate Python plugin guide.
  • Installation options:
    • curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/grafana/agento11y/main/plugins/agento11y/scripts/install.sh | sh
    • brew install grafana/grafana/agento11y
    • go install github.com/grafana/agento11y/plugins/agento11y/cmd/agento11y@latest
  • After installation, run agento11y login and launch an agent, e.g., agento11y codex.
  • The Coding Agent Observability guide covers all install options, configuration, and supported agents.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Instrument agents with SDKs available for Go, Python, JS, .NET, Java.
  • For custom app or agent code, use the agento11y-instrument agent skill:
    • Install gcx CLI: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/grafana/gcx/main/scripts/install.sh | sh or brew install gcx.
    • Install skill: gcx agent skills install agento11y-instrument.
    • Skill inspects code, applies SDK with small diffs after confirmation, and verifies data with gcx agento11y.
    • If agent does not support skills, give llms.txt and ask it to instrument.
    • Alternatively, use the onboarding wizard in the Agent Observability plugin.
  • Set AGENTO11Y_* environment variables and construct the client:
    • JS: import { Agento11yClient } from "@grafana/agento11y"; const client = new Agento11yClient();
    • Python: from agento11y import Client; client = Client()
    • Go: client := agento11y.NewClient(agento11y.Config{})

🚀 Availability

  • All SDKs and plugins are open source and available in the Grafana GitHub repo.
  • Supported agents include Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Vibe, experimental Kiro CLI, and others.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Enables monitoring of generations, tools, cost, traces, and evaluations across coding agents in one place.
  • Helps observe usage, cost, tokens, and tools across agents.
  • Allows developers to instrument their own apps or agents with minimal code changes.

#Grafana #Observability #AIagents #OpenSource #SDKs

Source: grafana/agento11y

item.title: Kiro Crew Offers a Persistent, Self-Evolving Development Workspace
item.description:
Kiro Crew Offers a Persistent, Self-Evolving Development Workspace

Kiro Crew is an open-source development workspace that runs locally or remotely on your hardware, with work designed to persist, learn, and evolve beyond a single session.

🔍 Overview

You can work with Kiro Crew through a desktop app, web dashboard, or CLI, and continue the same work through connection tools such as Slack and Discord.

🧩 How it works

  • Multi-step tasks can run unattended.
  • Recurring jobs run on a schedule.
  • Heartbeats monitor systems until something needs attention.
  • Kiro Crew Apps adapt the workspace to a specific job, combining a purpose-built interface with agents, skills, schedules, integrations, and backend services.

⚙️ Setup and updates

Kiro Crew can be run in several ways:

  • Use the desktop app, which includes automatic updates.
  • Install it on a machine or remote host with a one-line install.
  • Use the Docker image for always-on servers.
  • Build it from source.

The default agent runs on kiro-cli, which must be installed and signed in to separately. On first launch, Kiro Crew checks for this prerequisite and links to the official setup guide if it is missing. Download links fetch the newest build on their channel, and the app updates itself on that same channel. The recommended channel is Stable unless there is a reason to choose another.

🚀 Availability

Kiro Crew is available for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Package options include:

Platform Package
macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) .dmg
Windows (x64) .exe
Linux (x86_64 or aarch64) .deb, .rpm, or AppImage

On Linux, the one-line install is the recommended starting point; a desktop package can be added for a native window and in-app updates.

#KiroCrew #AIAgents #OpenSource #DevTools

Source: kirodotdev/KiroCrew

item.title: MATE and OpenAgent Add Production Orchestration and Visual Workflows
item.description:
MATE and OpenAgent Add Production Orchestration and Visual Workflows

Two new AI development platforms, MATE and OpenAgent, have emerged to address the complexity of moving from single-agent experiments to production-grade multi-agent systems. MATE serves as a control layer that adds operational capabilities like versioning and cost tracking without requiring changes to the underlying agent code. Simultaneously, OpenAgent provides a full-stack platform for building, orchestrating, and publishing AI applications with deep reasoning loops and visual workflow authoring.

🧩 MATE: The Production Control Layer

MATE is a self-hosted, multi-agent orchestration engine built on Google ADK or LangGraph. It is designed to manage agent hierarchies, tool attachments, and prompt editing on a visual canvas. The platform supports any of 50+ LLM providers and includes persistent memory, web dashboard capabilities, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

Key Operational Features

  • Configuration Management: Prompts, models, and user access permissions can be changed from a dashboard without code changes or redeployments.
  • Versioning and Rollback: Every configuration change is live, versioned, and allows for one-click rollback to any previous state.
  • Cost Tracking: Model calls are priced in US dollars as they are logged, supporting budgets that can warn or block based on spend.
  • Monitoring and Alerts: The system includes audit logs, guardrails, and alerts sent to Slack, Discord, email, or webhooks.
  • Trace Replay: A feature that plays back execution on a canvas, showing the order agents ran, hand-offs to sub-agents, models used, duration, and fallback usage.
  • Integration Options: Offers an embeddable chat widget, an OpenAI-compatible API, A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol support, and serves every agent as an MCP server.

Deployment and Case Studies

MATE can be deployed via Docker using the command docker run -d -p 8000:8000 -e AUTH_PASSWORD=change-me -e GOOGLE_API_KEY=your-key ghcr.io/antiv/mate:latest. The platform has been adopted by MVP-Soft, LLC, a US software consultancy, and Goal Navigator, which runs on MATE in production. Created by Ivan Antonijević, MATE also features a murder mystery demo and a browser-based wizard for provisioning agents, with an interface available in Serbian.

🖼️ OpenAgent: Visual Workflows and Deep Reasoning

OpenAgent is an end-to-end AI agent platform described as a full-stack solution for teams building AI applications. It combines a Flask backend with LangChain/LangGraph and a Vue 3 frontend workspace. The repository includes Celery workers, visual workflow authoring, dataset management, and public app publishing via OpenAPI.

Platform Capabilities

  • Visual Workflow Design: Users can design workflows using nodes for LLMs, tool calls, dataset retrieval, code execution, HTTP requests, branching, text processing, and structured parameter extraction.
  • Deep Research Mode: Allows apps to decompose complex tasks and coordinate capabilities across multi-step execution for scenarios requiring deep reasoning.
  • Knowledge and Retrieval: Supports RAG, semantic retrieval, full-text retrieval, and hybrid retrieval using Weaviate and FAISS.
  • Publishing and Delivery: Exposes published apps over REST and SSE through POST /api/openapi/chat.
  • Model Integrations: Compatible with OpenAI, Atlas Cloud, DeepSeek, Grok, Google, Moonshot, Tongyi, Wenxin, Ollama, and Zhipu. Atlas Cloud integration is configured via ATLASCLOUD_API_KEY and ATLASCLOUD_API_BASE.

⚙️ Technical Architecture Comparison

Feature MATE OpenAgent
Core Framework Google ADK, LangGraph LangChain, LangGraph
Backend Self-hosted Docker Python, Flask, Celery, Redis, PostgreSQL
Frontend Web Dashboard Vue 3, Vite, TailwindCSS, Pinia, Vue Flow
Primary Focus Agent orchestration, cost control, RBAC Visual workflows, RAG, deep reasoning loops
Model Providers 50+ LLM providers OpenAI, DeepSeek, Grok, Google, and others
Deployment Docker container Docker Compose, Nginx

💡 Why It Matters

A single agent in a notebook is easy to manage, but a hierarchy of agents serving real users introduces significant operational complexity. Without a control layer, tweaking a prompt requires editing code, committing changes, and redeploying the entire system. Additionally, teams often cannot easily identify which specific agent or token type (prompt, response, or reasoning) is consuming their budget. MATE addresses this by acting as a control layer that adds production necessities like versioning and cost visibility without touching the agent code. OpenAgent extends this utility by providing a dedicated workspace for drafting, publishing, and analyzing AI apps, allowing natural-language requirements to be turned into new creation flows.

#AIAgents #Orchestration #LangGraph #LLM #DevOps

Source: antiv/mate Source: Haohao-end/openagent

item.title: NVIDIA Launches Nemotron for Science to Accelerate Agentic Scientific Workloads

Step Tool Description
Environment NeMo Gym Supplies infrastructure for reinforcement learning (RL).

item.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Achieves 10× Agentic Throughput Per Kilowatt in MLPerf Endpoints v1.0
item.description:
NVIDIA Vera Rubin Achieves 10× Agentic Throughput Per Kilowatt in MLPerf Endpoints v1.0

NVIDIA released provisional results for its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform in the MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 benchmark, showing more than 10× the agentic throughput per kilowatt compared to the verified GB300 NVL72 while maintaining a minimum end‑to‑end interactivity of 50 tokens per second per user.

🔍 Overview

  • Agentic workloads are demanding more from inference systems.
  • AI agents carry growing conversation histories across turns and generate a mix of reasoning, tool calls, and responses.
  • Inference systems must support users at scale while remaining responsive.
  • The MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 dataset captures coding trajectories that accumulate history over many turns and enterprise workflows that reuse shared instructions, tool definitions, and business rules.

🧩 How It Works

  • The benchmark evaluates serving capacity and responsiveness using coding and enterprise workflows through API endpoints.
  • During performance runs, generated tool calls and workflow intent are checked against reference values.
  • Separate SWE‑bench Verified evaluations assess end‑to‑end task‑solving capability.
  • These checks evaluate whether faster serving preserves model quality.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Vera Rubin NVL72 (32 accelerators)
    • Run 9: concurrency = 1,024 queries
    • TTFT P90 = 4,673.9 ms
    • System TPS = 41,414.2 tokens/sec
    • E2E average interactivity = 50.4 tokens/sec per user
    • Operating power = 100.89 kW
  • GB300 NVL72 (48 accelerators)
    • Run 6: concurrency = 48 queries
    • TTFT P90 = 2,305.1 ms
    • System TPS = 2,210.4 tokens/sec
    • E2E average interactivity = 56.2 tokens/sec per user
    • Operating power = 60 kW

📊 Performance Results for Model Variants

  • Kimi K3
    • Vera Rubin: run 9, 1,024 queries, 41,414.2 TPS, 50.4 interactivity, 100.89 kW
    • GB300: run 6, 48 queries, 2,210.4 TPS, 56.2 interactivity, 60 kW
  • DeepSeek‑V4.1‑Flash
    • Vera Rubin: run 6, 1,408 queries, 272,711.7 TPS, 294.49 interactivity, 75.67 kW
    • GB300: run 1, 16 queries, 3,054.0 TPS, 288.65 interactivity, 7.50 kW
  • Qwen3.6‑35B‑A3B
    • Vera Rubin: run 8, 320 queries, 47,785.5 TPS, 411.9 interactivity, 12.61 kW
    • GB300: run 2, 36 queries, 5,960.4 TPS, 531.6 interactivity, 7.50 kW

📈 Tradeoff Curve

  • Figure 2 shows the tradeoff between throughput per provisioned kilowatt and E2E interactivity across at least seven concurrency levels per curve.
  • The curves illustrate how much throughput each system delivers at a given responsiveness requirement.

🔬 Verification Status

  • GB300 results are verified by the MLCommons Association.
  • Vera Rubin results are provisional.
  • Pending MLCommons Association verification, results may change.

#MLPerf #NVIDIA #Inference #AgenticWorkloads #Throughput

Source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Leads Agentic Inference Performance on MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: open-computer-use expands platform support and adds macOS Locked Use
